tr.en: Carried through many peoples and over many seas,
tr.it: Portato attraverso molte genti e molti mari,
tr.es: Llevado a través de muchos pueblos y muchos mares,

tr.en: I come, brother, to these sad rites for the dead,
tr.it: giungo, fratello, a queste misere offerte funebri,
tr.es: llego, hermano, a estas tristes ofrendas fúnebres,

tr.en: to present you with the last gift owed to the dead
tr.it: per farti l'ultimo dono che si deve ai morti
tr.es: para ofrecerte el último don que se debe a los muertos

tr.en: and to speak, in vain, to your silent ashes.
tr.it: e parlare invano alla tua cenere muta.
tr.es: y hablar en vano a tus cenizas mudas.

tr.en: since Fortune has taken you, you yourself, away from me,
tr.it: poiché la sorte mi ha strappato proprio te,
tr.es: ya que la fortuna me ha arrebatado a ti mismo,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. voc. sg. m.

tr.en: alas, poor brother, so unjustly taken from me,
tr.it: ahimè, povero fratello, a me tolto ingiustamente,
tr.es: ¡ay, pobre hermano, que injustamente me fuiste arrebatado!

tr.en: now nonetheless, meanwhile, these offerings, which by the ancient custom of our forefathers
tr.it: ora tuttavia, intanto, queste offerte che per antica usanza degli avi
tr.es: ahora, sin embargo, entretanto, estas ofrendas, que por antigua costumbre de los mayores

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. pl. n.

tr.en: are handed over as a sad gift at the rites for the dead—
tr.it: si offrono come triste dono nei riti funebri,
tr.es: se entregan como triste don en los ritos fúnebres,

tr.en: accept them, streaming with a brother's many tears,
tr.it: accoglile, tutte bagnate di pianto fraterno,
tr.es: acéptalas, empapadas de abundante llanto fraterno,

tr.en: and for ever, brother, hail and farewell.
tr.it: e per sempre, fratello, salve e addio.
tr.es: y para siempre, hermano, salve y adiós.

notes.n: ōdī 'I hate' exists only in perfect forms but has present meaning (like meminī 'I remember'). quārē 'for what reason, why' (quā rē) became French car 'because'. faciam is subjunctive in an indirect question.

nescio is scanned with a short final o. fierī is the infinitive of fīō 'happen, be done': 'I feel (that it) is happening'. excrucior is passive, literally 'I am put on the cross' (ex + cruciō, from crux → Italian croce, Spanish cruz, French croix); hence English excruciating.
vectus is the perfect participle of vehō 'carry': 'having been carried'. The pattern multās … gentēs / multa … aequora makes the line itself feel long, like the journey.

īnferiae are offerings to the dead (cf. īnferī 'those below'). frāter → French frère, Romanian frate, Italian frate 'friar' (the everyday word being the diminutive fratello); Spanish and Portuguese replaced it with hermano, irmão, from germānus 'of the same stock'.
ut + imperfect subjunctive (dōnārem, adloquerer) expresses purpose: 'in order to present … and speak'. dōnāre aliquem aliquā rē 'to present someone with something'.

cinis is normally masculine, but Catullus makes it feminine (mūtam … cinerem). It lives on in Italian cenere and French cendre; Spanish ceniza comes from a derivative. mūtus → Italian muto, Spanish mudo, French muet.
tētē is an emphatic, doubled tē. abstulit is the perfect of auferō (ab + ferō) with the irregular stem tul-: auferō, auferre, abstulī, ablātum.
adempte is the vocative of the participle ademptus (adimō 'take away'), agreeing with frāter; mihi is a dative of separation, 'from me'.
haec is the object of accipe two lines later. The relative clause is tucked in early: prīscō quae mōre = quae prīscō mōre.
avē 'hail' and valē 'be well, farewell' are imperatives: the Roman greeting and leave-taking spoken together at the grave. valēre lives on in Italian valere, Spanish valer, French valoir 'be worth'.

title: In the Beginning
orig: In prīncipiō creāvit Deus caelum et terram
author: Jerome (Vulgate)
intro: Between about AD 390 and 405 Jerome translated the Hebrew Bible into Latin; his version, the Vulgate ('common edition'), was the Bible of western Europe for over a thousand years. Its simple, repetitive syntax—full of et and of Hebrew turns of phrase—shaped medieval Latin and, through it, the religious vocabulary of every Romance language. These verses tell the first two days of creation.

tr.en: In the beginning God created heaven and earth.
tr.it: In principio Dio creò il cielo e la terra.
tr.es: En el principio creó Dios el cielo y la tierra.
tr.fr: Au commencement, Dieu créa le ciel et la terre.
tr.pt: No princípio, Deus criou o céu e a terra.

tr.en: Now the earth was empty and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep:
tr.it: Ora la terra era informe e vuota, e le tenebre erano sopra la faccia dell'abisso:
tr.es: La tierra estaba vacía y desierta, y había tinieblas sobre la faz del abismo:
tr.fr: Or la terre était vide et déserte, et les ténèbres étaient sur la face de l'abîme :
tr.pt: Ora, a terra era vazia e deserta, e as trevas estavam sobre a face do abismo:

tr.en: and the Spirit of God was moving over the waters.
tr.it: e lo spirito di Dio aleggiava sulle acque.
tr.es: y el espíritu de Dios se movía sobre las aguas.
tr.fr: et l'esprit de Dieu planait au-dessus des eaux.
tr.pt: e o espírito de Deus pairava sobre as águas.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: And God said: Let there be light. And light came to be.
tr.it: E Dio disse: Sia fatta la luce. E la luce fu fatta.
tr.es: Y dijo Dios: Hágase la luz. Y la luz se hizo.
tr.fr: Et Dieu dit : Que la lumière soit. Et la lumière fut.
tr.pt: E Deus disse: Faça-se a luz. E a luz foi feita.

tr.en: And God saw the light, that it was good: and he divided the light from the darkness.
tr.it: E Dio vide che la luce era buona: e separò la luce dalle tenebre.
tr.es: Y vio Dios que la luz era buena: y separó la luz de las tinieblas.
tr.fr: Et Dieu vit que la lumière était bonne : et il sépara la lumière des ténèbres.
tr.pt: E Deus viu que a luz era boa: e separou a luz das trevas.

tr.en: And he called the light Day, and the darkness Night:
tr.it: E chiamò la luce Giorno, e le tenebre Notte:
tr.es: Y llamó a la luz Día, y a las tinieblas Noche:
tr.fr: Et il appela la lumière Jour, et les ténèbres Nuit :
tr.pt: E chamou à luz Dia, e às trevas Noite:

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. n. + -que

tr.en: and there was evening and morning, one day.
tr.it: e fu sera e fu mattina: un giorno.
tr.es: y hubo tarde y mañana: un día.
tr.fr: et il y eut un soir et un matin : un jour.
tr.pt: e houve tarde e manhã: um dia.

tr.en: God also said: Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters: and let it divide waters from waters.
tr.it: Disse anche Dio: Sia fatto un firmamento in mezzo alle acque: e separi le acque dalle acque.
tr.es: Dijo también Dios: Hágase un firmamento en medio de las aguas, y separe unas aguas de otras.
tr.fr: Dieu dit encore : Qu'il y ait un firmament au milieu des eaux, et qu'il sépare les eaux d'avec les eaux.
tr.pt: Disse também Deus: Faça-se um firmamento no meio das águas, e separe águas de águas.

tr.en: And God made the firmament, and divided the waters that were under the firmament
tr.it: E Dio fece il firmamento, e separò le acque che erano sotto il firmamento
tr.es: Y Dios hizo el firmamento, y separó las aguas que estaban debajo del firmamento
tr.fr: Et Dieu fit le firmament, et il sépara les eaux qui étaient sous le firmament
tr.pt: E Deus fez o firmamento, e separou as águas que estavam debaixo do firmamento

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. n.

tr.en: from those that were above the firmament. And so it was.
tr.it: da quelle che erano sopra il firmamento. E così avvenne.
tr.es: de las que estaban sobre el firmamento. Y así fue.
tr.fr: de celles qui étaient au-dessus du firmament. Et il en fut ainsi.
tr.pt: das que estavam acima do firmamento. E assim se fez.

tr.en: And God called the firmament Heaven:
tr.it: E Dio chiamò il firmamento Cielo:
tr.es: Y Dios llamó al firmamento Cielo:
tr.fr: Et Dieu appela le firmament Ciel :
tr.pt: E Deus chamou ao firmamento Céu:

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. n.

tr.en: and there was evening and morning, a second day.
tr.it: e fu sera e fu mattina: secondo giorno.
tr.es: y hubo tarde y mañana: día segundo.
tr.fr: et il y eut un soir et un matin : second jour.
tr.pt: e houve tarde e manhã: segundo dia.

notes.n: In prīncipiō → Italian in principio, Portuguese no princípio; French says au commencement. Deus has no article: Latin had none, while every Romance language created one from ille or ipse (il, el, le, o).
inānis et vacua 'empty and void' renders the Hebrew tohu va-bohu, which French keeps as tohu-bohu 'chaos'. tenebrae exists only in the plural. abyssus is a Greek loan (ἄβυσσος 'bottomless').
spīritus 'breath, wind, spirit' (spīrō 'breathe') → Italian spirito, Spanish espíritu, French esprit. ferēbātur, literally 'was being carried'.
Fīat is the present subjunctive of fīō 'become, be made': 'let it be made'. facta est is perfect: 'was made'. lūx → Italian luce, Spanish and Portuguese luz; French lumière comes from lūmināria.

quod esset bona: classical Latin would say vīdit lūcem esse bonam (accusative + infinitive). Late Latin increasingly used a clause with quod 'that'—the construction that became Romance che, que: vide che la luce era buona, vio que la luz era buena.

nox, noctis → Italian notte, Spanish noche, French nuit, Portuguese noite, Romanian noapte—a textbook case of what Latin -ct- became in each language. diēs → Spanish día; Italian giorno and French jour come from diurnum 'daily'.

factum est 'it came about' = 'there was'. vespere 'in the evening' and māne 'in the morning' are adverbial. diēs ūnus 'one day' follows the Hebrew, which uses the cardinal number for the first day. māne lives on in Spanish mañana (from *māneāna) and French demain.
dīvidat is a jussive subjunctive, 'let it divide'. firmāmentum 'something made firm' renders the Hebrew word for the vault of the sky, imagined as a solid dome holding back the waters above.
Et factum est ita 'and it was done so' is the refrain repeated after each act of creation. ab hīs 'from those (waters)'.
secundus 'second' comes from sequor 'follow': the one that follows. Italian secondo, Spanish segundo, French second; English second is borrowed from it.

title: Let Us Live and Love
author: Catullus
intro: Gaius Valerius Catullus (c. 84–54 BC) wrote a cycle of poems to 'Lesbia', a pseudonym usually identified with the aristocratic Clodia. In these eleven-syllable lines he sets the brevity of human life against the endless return of the sun, and answers with a frenzy of kisses. The 'thousand kisses' have been imitated ever since, from Renaissance love poetry to Ben Jonson's 'Come, my Celia'.

tr.en: Let us live, my Lesbia, and let us love,
tr.it: Viviamo, mia Lesbia, e amiamo,
tr.es: Vivamos, Lesbia mía, y amemos,

tr.en: and all the mutterings of over-strict old men
tr.it: e le chiacchiere dei vecchi troppo severi
tr.es: y las habladurías de los viejos demasiado severos,

tr.en: let us value at a single penny!
tr.it: stimiamole tutte quante un soldo!
tr.es: ¡valorémoslas todas en un solo céntimo!

tr.en: Suns can set and come back again:
tr.it: I soli possono tramontare e ritornare:
tr.es: Los soles pueden ponerse y volver:

tr.en: for us, once our brief light has set,
tr.it: per noi, una volta tramontata la breve luce,
tr.es: para nosotros, una vez que se pone la breve luz,

tr.en: there is one never-ending night to be slept.
tr.it: c'è un'unica notte eterna da dormire.
tr.es: hay que dormir una sola noche eterna.

tr.en: Give me a thousand kisses, then a hundred,
tr.it: Dammi mille baci, poi cento,
tr.es: Dame mil besos, después cien,

tr.en: then another thousand, then a second hundred,
tr.it: poi altri mille, poi altri cento,
tr.es: luego otros mil, luego otros cien,

tr.en: then yet another thousand, then a hundred.
tr.it: poi ancora altri mille, poi cento.
tr.es: después otros mil más, después cien.

tr.en: Then, when we have made many thousands,
tr.it: Poi, quando ne avremo fatte molte migliaia,
tr.es: Luego, cuando hayamos hecho muchos miles,

tr.en: we will muddle up the count, so that we don't know it,
tr.it: ne scompiglieremo il conto, per non saperlo,
tr.es: embrollaremos la cuenta, para no saberla,

tr.en: or so that no evil person can cast the evil eye on us
tr.it: o perché nessun malvagio possa gettarci il malocchio
tr.es: o para que ningún malvado pueda echarnos mal de ojo

tr.en: when he knows that there are so many kisses.
tr.it: sapendo che i baci sono tanti.
tr.es: al saber que hay tantos besos.

notes.n: Vīvāmus … amēmus are hortatory subjunctives: 'let us live, let us love'. The Latin present subjunctive survives as the Romance 'let's' form: Italian viviamo, amiamo; Spanish vivamos, amemos.
sevēriōrum is comparative in the sense 'too strict, rather strict'. rūmor 'talk, gossip' → Italian rumore and Spanish rumor; French rumeur.
ūnius assis is a genitive of value: 'at (the price of) one as', the smallest copper coin. Catullus scans ūnius with a short i, a common poetic licence.
occidere 'to fall, to set' (ob + cadō), not occīdere 'to kill'. The setting sun gave the Occident, Italian and Spanish occidente; redīre is red- + īre 'go back'.
nox … dormienda (est) nōbīs is a passive periphrastic: gerundive + sum with a dative of the agent—'a night must be slept by us'. Note the stark contrast lūx / nox at the ends of two lines.
bāsium was a colloquial word that ousted the older ōsculum: Italian bacio, Spanish beso, French baiser, Portuguese beijo all descend from it. mī is the contracted form of mihi.

fēcerīmus is future perfect: 'when we shall have made'. mīlia, the plural of mīlle, behaves as a neuter noun (mīlia bāsiōrum 'thousands of kisses'); Italian mille / mila keeps the same singular–plural contrast.
conturbāre is an accountant's word: to throw the accounts into confusion (also 'to go bankrupt'). The lovers wipe the abacus clean so that no total can be known. illa refers to the mīlia.

invidēre, literally 'to look upon (with the evil eye)': to know the exact count of someone's blessings was believed to give power to bewitch them. Its noun invidia → English envy, Italian invidia, Spanish envidia.
tantum … bāsiōrum: neuter tantum 'so much' with a partitive genitive, 'so great a number of kisses'. cum + subjunctive here is 'when' with a causal colour.

title: O Fortune
author: Anonymous (Carmina Burana)
intro: The Carmina Burana are some 250 medieval Latin and German songs preserved in a manuscript of about 1230, discovered in 1803 at the Bavarian monastery of Benediktbeuern. Their anonymous authors—wandering scholars and clerics—wrote rhyming, stress-based verse rather than classical quantitative metre. This lament on the Wheel of Fortune became world-famous through Carl Orff's setting of 1937; each line here combines two short rhyming lines and a longer one.

tr.en: O Fortune, like the moon, ever changing in your state,
tr.it: O Fortuna, come la luna, mutevole nel tuo stato,
tr.es: Oh Fortuna, como la luna, variable en tu estado,

tr.en: you are always waxing or waning; hateful life
tr.it: sempre cresci o cali; la vita odiosa
tr.es: siempre creces o menguas; la vida detestable

tr.en: now is harsh and then soothes the mind's keen edge, as a game;
tr.it: ora è dura e poi lenisce, per gioco, l'acume della mente;
tr.es: ahora es dura y luego alivia, por juego, la agudeza de la mente;

tr.en: poverty and power alike it melts like ice.
tr.it: povertà e potere li scioglie come ghiaccio.
tr.es: pobreza y poder los derrite como el hielo.

tr.en: Fate, monstrous and empty, you are a turning wheel,
tr.it: Sorte mostruosa e vuota, tu sei una ruota che gira,
tr.es: Suerte monstruosa y vacía, tú eres una rueda que gira,

tr.en: a wicked state, a hollow well-being, always ready to dissolve;
tr.it: condizione maligna, salvezza vana, sempre pronta a dissolversi;
tr.es: estado maligno, vana salud, siempre a punto de disolverse;

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.
perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: shadowed and veiled, you bear down on me too;
tr.it: adombrata e velata, incombi anche su di me;
tr.es: en sombra y velada, me acosas también a mí;

tr.en: now, through your game, I offer my bare back to your cruelty.
tr.it: ora, per il tuo gioco, offro la schiena nuda alla tua crudeltà.
tr.es: ahora, por tu juego, ofrezco la espalda desnuda a tu crueldad.

notes.n: Fortūna, goddess of chance, is compared to the moon: lūna → Italian and Spanish luna, French lune, Portuguese lua, Romanian lună. statū is an ablative of respect, 'changeable in state'. Macrons are added here only as a guide: the medieval poet counted stresses and rhymes, not long and short syllables.

crēscis aut dēcrēscis: the waxing and waning moon. crēscō → Italian crescere, Spanish crecer, French croître. Adjectives in -bilis (variābilis, dētestābilis, volūbilis, dissolūbilis) supply many of the rhymes.

lūdō 'for sport, as a game' is best taken as a dative of purpose (some read it as an ablative, 'in play'). aciēs mentis is literally 'the cutting edge of the mind'. cūrāre 'take care of, heal' → Italian curare, Spanish curar.

egestātem, potestātem: two rhyming nouns in -tās, -tātis, the suffix that became Italian -tà, Spanish -dad, French -té. potestās survives as Italian podestà, the chief magistrate of medieval Italian cities. glaciēs → French glace, Italian ghiaccio (from *glacia).

Fortune is now addressed as Sors 'lot, fate', and called rota volūbilis, the Wheel of Fortune that lifts kings up and throws them down. rota → Italian ruota, Spanish rueda, French roue, Portuguese roda, Romanian roată.
status malus, vāna salūs are nominatives in apposition to 'you' (Fortune). salūs 'health, safety, salvation' → Italian salute, Spanish salud, French salut.
michi is the usual medieval spelling of mihi: the h had come to be pronounced like ch. nīteris is from the deponent nītor 'lean on, press upon'.

dorsum nūdum ferō 'I bring my naked back', as if to the lash; tuī sceleris depends loosely on the whole phrase, '(exposed) to your wickedness'. dorsum → Italian dosso, French dos; nūdus → Italian nudo, Spanish desnudo, French nu.

title: Six Epigrams
author: Martial
intro: Marcus Valerius Martialis (c. AD 40–104), a Spaniard from Bilbilis, made the short, barbed epigram his speciality in the Rome of the Flavian emperors. Most of his poems are elegiac couplets that save the sting for the last words. These six include his own verdict on his book and the original of the English rhyme 'I do not love thee, Dr Fell'.

tr.en: There are good things, there are some middling ones, there are more bad ones
tr.it: Ci sono cose buone, alcune mediocri, e di più quelle cattive
tr.es: Hay cosas buenas, algunas mediocres y más aún malas

tr.en: in what you read here: there's no other way, Avitus, to make a book.
tr.it: in ciò che leggi qui: un libro, Avito, non si fa altrimenti.
tr.es: en lo que lees aquí: un libro, Avito, no se hace de otro modo.

tr.en: I don't love you, Sabidius, nor can I say why:
tr.it: Non ti amo, Sabidio, né so dire perché:
tr.es: No te quiero, Sabidio, ni sé decir por qué:

tr.en: this much only I can say: I don't love you.
tr.it: questo solo posso dire: non ti amo.
tr.es: solo esto puedo decir: no te quiero.

tr.en: Diaulus was a doctor until lately; now he's an undertaker:
tr.it: Fino a poco fa Diaulo era medico, ora è becchino:
tr.es: Hasta hace poco Diaulo era médico, ahora es enterrador:

tr.en: what he does as an undertaker, he had already done as a doctor.
tr.it: quello che fa da becchino, lo faceva già da medico.
tr.es: lo que hace de enterrador, ya lo hacía de médico.

tr.en: You ask, Linus, what my farm at Nomentum yields me?
tr.it: Mi chiedi, Lino, che cosa mi renda il podere di Nomento?
tr.es: ¿Me preguntas, Lino, qué me rinde mi finca de Nomento?

tr.en: This is what the farm yields me: I don't see you, Linus.
tr.it: Ecco che cosa mi rende il podere: non vedo te, Lino.
tr.es: Esto me rinde la finca: no te veo a ti, Lino.

tr.en: Cinna is said to be writing little verses against me.
tr.it: Si dice che Cinna scriva versetti contro di me.
tr.es: Se dice que Cinna escribe versitos contra mí.

tr.en: A man whose poems nobody reads does not write.
tr.it: Non scrive chi ha versi che nessuno legge.
tr.es: No escribe aquel cuyos versos nadie lee.

tr.en: Thais has black teeth, Laecania snow-white ones.
tr.it: Taide ha i denti neri, Lecania bianchi come la neve.
tr.es: Tais tiene los dientes negros; Lecania, blancos como la nieve.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. acc. pl. m.

tr.en: What's the reason? The latter has bought ones, the former her own.
tr.it: Qual è la ragione? Questa li ha comprati, quella ha i suoi.
tr.es: ¿Cuál es la razón? Esta los tiene comprados; aquella, los suyos.

notes.n: Epigram 1.16. plūra is the neuter plural of the comparative plūs 'more', which serves as the comparative of multus. quaedam 'certain (things)' is from quīdam.
fit 'is made, comes about' (fīō). liber 'book' (short i, genitive librī) → Italian and Spanish libro, French livre; do not confuse it with līber 'free'.

Epigram 1.32. Sabidī is the vocative of Sabidius (nouns in -ius have vocative -ī, like fīlī, Lūcīlī). Around 1680 Tom Brown turned it into 'I do not love thee, Dr Fell, / The reason why I cannot tell'. In both lines the metre needs amo with a short final o, as often in poets of this period (compare vispillo in 1.47). amō, possum, dīcere → Italian amo, posso, dire; Spanish amo, puedo, decir.
Epigram 1.47. A vispillo (also vespillō) carried out the corpses of the poor at night. The final o is scanned short here, as often in Martial's time.
The joke turns on the pluperfect fēcerat 'had (already) done' and on et = 'also': as a doctor he was already supplying corpses. medicus → Italian medico, Spanish médico.
Epigram 2.38. reddat is subjunctive in an indirect question after quaeris. Nōmentānus 'at Nomentum', a town north-east of Rome where Martial had a small farm. Line is the vocative of Linus.
reddō 'give back, yield' → Italian rendere, Spanish rendir, French rendre (through a form *rendere influenced by prendere).
Epigram 3.9. nārrātur scrībere: personal passive with infinitive, 'he is said to write'. versiculus is a diminutive of versus 'verse'; the -culus suffix belittles.
The subject of scrībit is the man described by the relative clause: '(he) whose poems nobody reads does not write'. cuius = 'whose'.
Epigram 5.43. niger → Italian nero, Spanish negro, French noir; niveus 'snowy' is from nix, nivis → Italian neve, Spanish nieve, French neige. dēns, dentis → dente, diente, dent.
haec … illa 'the latter … the former': haec points to the nearer name (Laecania), illa to the farther one (Thais). ēmptōs (from emō 'buy') agrees with dentēs understood: Laecania's teeth are false.

title: The Nativity
orig: Factum est autem in diēbus illīs
author: Jerome (Vulgate)
intro: In AD 382–384 Jerome revised the older Latin translations of the Gospels against the Greek, at the request of Pope Damasus. Luke's account of the birth of Jesus, read every Christmas for sixteen centuries, gave the Romance languages much of their Christmas vocabulary, from presepe to Natale. The angels' song in the last line became the opening of the Gloria of the Mass.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. n.

tr.en: Now it came to pass in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be registered.
tr.it: In quei giorni un editto di Cesare Augusto ordinò che si facesse il censimento di tutta la terra.
tr.es: Sucedió en aquellos días que salió un edicto de César Augusto para que se empadronara todo el mundo.
tr.fr: En ces jours-là, parut un édit de César Auguste ordonnant de recenser toute la terre.
tr.pt: Aconteceu naqueles dias que saiu um édito de César Augusto para que se recenseasse todo o mundo.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: This first registration was made by Quirinius, governor of Syria:
tr.it: Questo primo censimento fu fatto da Quirinio, governatore della Siria:
tr.es: Este primer censo lo hizo Quirino, gobernador de Siria:
tr.fr: Ce premier recensement fut fait par Quirinius, gouverneur de Syrie :
tr.pt: Este primeiro recenseamento foi feito por Quirino, governador da Síria:

tr.en: and all went to be registered, each to his own town.
tr.it: e tutti andavano a farsi registrare, ciascuno nella propria città.
tr.es: e iban todos a empadronarse, cada uno a su ciudad.
tr.fr: et tous allaient se faire inscrire, chacun dans sa ville.
tr.pt: e todos iam alistar-se, cada um na sua cidade.

tr.en: And Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, into Judaea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem,
tr.it: Anche Giuseppe salì dalla Galilea, dalla città di Nazaret, in Giudea, alla città di Davide chiamata Betlemme,
tr.es: También José subió de Galilea, de la ciudad de Nazaret, a Judea, a la ciudad de David que se llama Belén,
tr.fr: Joseph aussi monta de Galilée, de la ville de Nazareth, en Judée, dans la ville de David appelée Bethléem,
tr.pt: Também José subiu da Galileia, da cidade de Nazaré, à Judeia, à cidade de David chamada Belém,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. abl. sg. f.

tr.en: because he was of the house and family of David, to be registered with Mary, his betrothed wife, who was with child.
tr.it: perché era della casa e della famiglia di Davide, per farsi registrare insieme a Maria, sua sposa promessa, che era incinta.
tr.es: porque era de la casa y familia de David, para empadronarse con María, su esposa prometida, que estaba encinta.
tr.fr: parce qu'il était de la maison et de la famille de David, afin de se faire inscrire avec Marie, son épouse promise, qui était enceinte.
tr.pt: por ser da casa e da família de David, para se alistar com Maria, sua esposa prometida, que estava grávida.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. n.
perf. pass. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: And it came to pass that while they were there, the days were completed for her to give birth.
tr.it: E avvenne che, mentre si trovavano lì, si compirono per lei i giorni del parto.
tr.es: Y sucedió que, estando ellos allí, se cumplieron los días de su parto.
tr.fr: Et pendant qu'ils étaient là, arriva le temps où elle devait enfanter.
tr.pt: E aconteceu que, estando eles ali, se completaram os dias em que ela devia dar à luz.

tr.en: And she gave birth to her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger,
tr.it: E diede alla luce il suo figlio primogenito, lo avvolse in fasce e lo adagiò in una mangiatoia,
tr.es: Y dio a luz a su hijo primogénito, lo envolvió en pañales y lo acostó en un pesebre,
tr.fr: Et elle mit au monde son fils premier-né, l'enveloppa de langes et le coucha dans une mangeoire,
tr.pt: E deu à luz o seu filho primogénito, envolveu-o em panos e deitou-o numa manjedoura,

tr.en: because there was no room for them in the inn.
tr.it: perché per loro non c'era posto nell'alloggio.
tr.es: porque no había sitio para ellos en la posada.
tr.fr: parce qu'il n'y avait pas de place pour eux dans l'hôtellerie.
tr.pt: porque não havia lugar para eles na hospedaria.

tr.en: And there were shepherds in that same region, staying awake and keeping the night watches over their flock.
tr.it: E in quella stessa regione c'erano dei pastori che vegliavano e facevano di notte la guardia al loro gregge.
tr.es: Y había en la misma región unos pastores que velaban y hacían por turnos la guardia nocturna sobre su rebaño.
tr.fr: Et il y avait dans la même région des bergers qui veillaient et montaient la garde de nuit auprès de leur troupeau.
tr.pt: E havia na mesma região uns pastores que velavam e guardavam durante a noite o seu rebanho.

tr.en: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood beside them, and the brightness of God shone all around them, and they were filled with great fear.
tr.it: Ed ecco, un angelo del Signore si presentò a loro, e lo splendore di Dio li avvolse di luce, e furono presi da grande timore.
tr.es: Y he aquí que un ángel del Señor se presentó ante ellos, y la claridad de Dios los envolvió con su luz, y tuvieron gran temor.
tr.fr: Et voici qu'un ange du Seigneur se tint près d'eux, et la clarté de Dieu les enveloppa de lumière, et ils furent saisis d'une grande crainte.
tr.pt: E eis que um anjo do Senhor se pôs junto deles, e a claridade de Deus os envolveu, e tiveram grande temor.

tr.en: And the angel said to them: Do not be afraid: for behold, I bring you good news of great joy, which will be for all the people:
tr.it: E l'angelo disse loro: Non temete: ecco, vi annuncio una grande gioia, che sarà per tutto il popolo:
tr.es: Y el ángel les dijo: No temáis, pues os anuncio una gran alegría, que lo será para todo el pueblo:
tr.fr: Et l'ange leur dit : Ne craignez pas, car voici que je vous annonce une grande joie, qui sera pour tout le peuple :
tr.pt: E o anjo disse-lhes: Não temais, pois eis que vos anuncio uma grande alegria, que o será para todo o povo:

tr.en: for today a Saviour has been born to you, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David.
tr.it: perché oggi vi è nato un Salvatore, che è il Cristo Signore, nella città di Davide.
tr.es: porque hoy os ha nacido un Salvador, que es Cristo el Señor, en la ciudad de David.
tr.fr: car aujourd'hui vous est né un Sauveur, qui est le Christ Seigneur, dans la ville de David.
tr.pt: porque hoje vos nasceu um Salvador, que é Cristo Senhor, na cidade de David.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. acc. sg. m.
perf. pass. ptcp. acc. sg. m.

tr.en: And this will be the sign for you: you will find an infant wrapped in swaddling cloths and laid in a manger.
tr.it: E questo sarà per voi il segno: troverete un bambino avvolto in fasce e deposto in una mangiatoia.
tr.es: Y esta será la señal para vosotros: encontraréis a un niño envuelto en pañales y acostado en un pesebre.
tr.fr: Et voici le signe qui vous est donné : vous trouverez un nouveau-né enveloppé de langes et couché dans une mangeoire.
tr.pt: E este será o sinal para vós: encontrareis um menino envolto em panos e deitado numa manjedoura.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying:
tr.it: E subito apparve con l'angelo una moltitudine dell'esercito celeste, che lodava Dio e diceva:
tr.es: Y de repente apareció junto al ángel una multitud del ejército celestial, que alababa a Dios y decía:
tr.fr: Et soudain il y eut avec l'ange une multitude de l'armée céleste, qui louait Dieu et disait :
tr.pt: E de repente apareceu com o anjo uma multidão do exército celeste, que louvava a Deus e dizia:

tr.en: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.
tr.it: Gloria a Dio nel più alto dei cieli, e pace in terra agli uomini di buona volontà.
tr.es: Gloria a Dios en las alturas, y en la tierra paz a los hombres de buena voluntad.
tr.fr: Gloire à Dieu au plus haut des cieux, et paix sur la terre aux hommes de bonne volonté.
tr.pt: Glória a Deus nas alturas, e paz na terra aos homens de boa vontade.

notes.n: Factum est … exiit 'it happened … (that) there went out': a Hebrew-style narrative opening (wayehi) that the Greek and Latin Bibles copy. dēscrīberētur 'should be enrolled' (in a census) is imperfect subjunctive after ēdictum, a clause of command.
profitērentur is from the deponent profiteor 'declare publicly', here 'register one's name and property' → profess, profession. singulī 'one by one, each'.
Hebrew names such as Ioseph, David, Nazareth and Bethlehem are indeclinable in the Vulgate: only the context shows their case. et here means 'also'.

eō quod 'for this reason, that' = 'because'. dēspōnsātā sibi uxōre praegnante: a string of ablatives after cum, 'with Mary, the wife betrothed to him, being pregnant'. dēspōnsāre 'betroth' → Spanish desposar, esposa; English spouse comes from spōnsus.
implētī sunt diēs ut pareret 'the days were fulfilled that she should give birth'. pariō 'give birth' → Spanish and Portuguese parir; Italian partorire is from the related parturiō.
pannus 'cloth, rag' → Italian panno, Spanish paño; Spanish pañales 'nappies'. praesēpium 'stall, manger' → Italian presepe/presepio, the Christmas crib scene, and Spanish pesebre.
erat eīs locus: dative of possession, 'they had no place'. dīversōrium 'inn, lodging' is from dēvertō 'turn aside (to stay the night)'.
pāstor 'shepherd' (from pāscō 'feed, graze') → Italian pastore, Spanish pastor, French pasteur. vigiliae noctis are the watches into which the night was divided.

ecce 'look!' is a favourite of Biblical Latin; fused with demonstratives it produced Italian questo, quello (eccu(m) istum, eccu(m) illum) and French ce (ecce hoc). timuērunt timōre magnō 'they feared with great fear', a Hebrew-style repetition.

Nōlīte timēre 'do not be afraid': nōlī / nōlīte + infinitive is the usual Latin negative command. ēvangelizō is a Greek loan (εὐαγγελίζομαι 'bring good news') → evangelize, Italian evangelizzare. gaudium → Spanish gozo; French joie (whence Italian gioia) comes from the plural gaudia.

nātus est 'has been born' (deponent nāscor). Italian Natale and Portuguese Natal 'Christmas' come from nātālis (diēs); Spanish Navidad from nātīvitās. salvātor (from salvāre 'save') → Italian salvatore, Spanish salvador, French sauveur.
īnfāns is literally 'not (yet) speaking' (in- + fārī 'speak'): a baby. French enfant and Italian and Spanish infante continue it.
laudantium, dīcentium are genitive plural participles agreeing in sense with the angels contained in multitūdō: a construction according to sense. mīlitia 'army, military service' → militia.

in altissimīs 'in the highest (places)', neuter plural superlative of altus. hominibus bonae voluntātis: genitive of quality, 'to men of good will' (that is, those on whom God's favour rests). These words open the Gloria of the Latin Mass.

title: The Wolf and the Lamb
orig: Ad rīvum eundem lupus et agnus vēnerant
author: Phaedrus
intro: Phaedrus, a freed slave of the emperor Augustus, put Aesop's Greek fables into Latin iambic verse in the early first century AD. This, the first fable of his first book, shows the powerful inventing pretexts to destroy the innocent, and ends with an explicit moral. Through medieval schoolbooks it reached La Fontaine, whose 'La raison du plus fort est toujours la meilleure' retells it.

tr.en: A wolf and a lamb had come to the same stream,
tr.it: Allo stesso ruscello erano giunti un lupo e un agnello,
tr.es: A un mismo arroyo habían llegado un lobo y un cordero,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: driven by thirst. Higher up stood the wolf,
tr.it: spinti dalla sete. Più in alto stava il lupo,
tr.es: empujados por la sed. Más arriba estaba el lobo,

tr.en: and the lamb far below. Then, by his greedy gullet
tr.it: e molto più in basso l'agnello. Allora, istigato dalla gola ingorda,
tr.es: y mucho más abajo el cordero. Entonces, azuzado por su voraz garganta,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: spurred on, the robber brought forward a pretext for a quarrel:
tr.it: il predone tirò fuori un pretesto per litigare:
tr.es: el bandido sacó un pretexto para la riña:

tr.en: “Why,” he said, “have you made the water muddy for me
tr.it: «Perché», disse, «mi hai intorbidito l'acqua
tr.es: «¿Por qué», dijo, «me has enturbiado el agua

tr.en: while I'm drinking?” The woolly one, frightened, answered:
tr.it: mentre bevo?». Il lanuto, timoroso, di rimando:
tr.es: mientras bebo?». El lanudo, temeroso, respondió:

tr.en: “How can I, please, do what you complain of, wolf?
tr.it: «Come posso, di grazia, fare ciò di cui ti lamenti, lupo?
tr.es: «¿Cómo puedo, por favor, hacer aquello de que te quejas, lobo?

tr.en: The water runs down from you to where I drink.”
tr.it: L'acqua scorre giù da te fino ai miei sorsi».
tr.es: El agua baja de ti hasta donde yo bebo».

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: Beaten back by the force of the truth, the wolf
tr.it: Respinto dalla forza della verità, quello
tr.es: Rechazado por la fuerza de la verdad, aquel

tr.en: said: “Six months ago you spoke ill of me.”
tr.it: disse: «Sei mesi fa hai parlato male di me».
tr.es: dijo: «Hace seis meses hablaste mal de mí».

tr.en: The lamb answered: “But I wasn't even born.”
tr.it: Rispose l'agnello: «Ma io non ero ancora nato».
tr.es: Respondió el cordero: «Pero si yo aún no había nacido».

tr.en: “Your father, by Hercules,” he said, “spoke ill of me”;
tr.it: «Tuo padre, per Ercole», disse quello, «ha parlato male di me»;
tr.es: «Tu padre, por Hércules», dijo aquel, «habló mal de mí»;

w: perf. pass. ptcp. acc. sg. m.

tr.en: and with that he seizes him and tears him apart in an unjust slaughter.
tr.it: e così lo afferra e lo sbrana, dandogli una morte ingiusta.
tr.es: y así lo atrapa y lo despedaza, dándole una muerte injusta.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: This fable was written because of those people
tr.it: Questa favola è stata scritta per quegli uomini
tr.es: Esta fábula se escribió por aquellos hombres

w: perf. pass. ptcp. abl. pl. f.

tr.en: who crush the innocent on invented pretexts.
tr.it: che con falsi pretesti opprimono gli innocenti.
tr.es: que con pretextos inventados oprimen a los inocentes.

notes.n: eundem is the accusative of īdem 'the same' (is + -dem). vēnerant is pluperfect: they 'had come'. lupus → Italian lupo, Spanish and Portuguese lobo, French loup, Romanian lup.
superior and īnferior (next line) are comparatives of superus 'upper' and īnferus 'lower'. The whole fable hangs on this geography: water flows downhill.
fauce improbā: the singular of faucēs 'throat, jaws', here 'greedy gullet'. improbus means 'shameless, insatiable'.

latrō 'robber' (originally 'mercenary') → Italian ladro, Spanish ladrón, French larron. iūrgiī causam intulit 'brought in a cause of quarrel', i.e. picked a fight. intulit is the perfect of īnferō (in + ferō).
bibentī is a present participle in the dative, agreeing with mihi: 'for me as I drink'. lāniger 'wool-bearing' (lāna + gerō) is a poetic name for the lamb, like Italian lanuto.
Quī here is an old adverb meaning 'how?', not the relative pronoun. quaesō 'I beg you, please'. quereris is the 2nd singular of the deponent queror 'complain' (→ English querulous).
ante hōs sex mēnsēs 'six months before these days', i.e. 'six months ago'. male dīcere 'speak ill' became Italian maledire, Spanish maldecir, French maudire 'curse'.
nātus … eram is the pluperfect of the deponent nāscor 'be born': 'I had not been born'. equidem 'for my part, truly'. The participle lives on in Italian nato, Spanish nacido, French né.
hercle 'by Hercules!' is a common Roman oath, mostly used by men.

correptum (from corripiō 'seize') agrees with the lamb understood: 'having seized him, he tears him'. lacerat is a vivid historic present. nex, necis is violent death (cf. necō 'kill', English internecine).

The moral at the end (epimythium). hominēs is separated from illōs by the verb, a word order (hyperbaton) common in verse. fābula → Italian favola, Spanish fábula; Spanish habla 'speech' is the inherited form of the same word.

title: Arms and the Man
author: Vergil
intro: Publius Vergilius Maro (70–19 BC) spent the last ten years of his life on the Aeneid, the epic of Aeneas' flight from burning Troy to Italy, where his descendants would found Rome. These opening hexameters announce the theme, name the angry goddess Juno as the hero's enemy and call on the Muse. For two thousand years they were the most memorized lines of Latin in Europe.

tr.en: I sing of arms and the man who first from the shores of Troy
tr.it: Canto le armi e l'uomo che per primo dalle spiagge di Troia
tr.es: Canto las armas y al hombre que, el primero, desde las costas de Troya

tr.en: came, an exile by fate, to Italy and the Lavinian
tr.it: giunse in Italia, profugo per volere del fato, e ai lidi
tr.es: llegó a Italia, prófugo por obra del hado, y a las playas

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: shores—much tossed about both on land and on the deep
tr.it: di Lavinio—molto sbattuto per terre e per mare
tr.es: de Lavinio—muy zarandeado por tierras y por mar

tr.en: by the power of the gods above, because of cruel Juno's unforgetting anger;
tr.it: dalla potenza dei celesti, per l'ira memore della crudele Giunone;
tr.es: por el poder de los dioses, a causa de la ira rencorosa de la cruel Juno;

tr.en: having suffered much in war as well, until he could found a city
tr.it: e molto avendo sofferto anche in guerra, finché fondasse una città
tr.es: y tras sufrir mucho también en la guerra, hasta poder fundar una ciudad

tr.en: and bring his gods into Latium; from him came the Latin race,
tr.it: e portare i suoi dèi nel Lazio; da lui la stirpe latina,
tr.es: y llevar sus dioses al Lacio; de él vienen la raza latina,

tr.en: the Alban fathers, and the walls of lofty Rome.
tr.it: i padri albani e le mura dell'alta Roma.
tr.es: los padres albanos y las murallas de la alta Roma.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. abl. sg. n.

tr.en: Muse, tell me the causes: what slight to her divine will,
tr.it: Musa, ricordami le cause: per quale offesa al suo nume,
tr.es: Musa, recuérdame las causas: por qué ofensa a su numen,

tr.en: or what grievance drove the queen of the gods to make a man
tr.it: o per quale dolore la regina degli dèi spinse a passare per tante sventure
tr.es: o por qué agravio la reina de los dioses obligó a pasar por tantas desgracias

tr.en: famous for his devotion roll through so many disasters and face so many toils.
tr.it: un uomo insigne per pietà, ad affrontare tante fatiche.
tr.es: a un hombre insigne por su piedad, a afrontar tantos trabajos.

tr.en: Can there be such great anger in the hearts of the gods?
tr.it: Possono gli animi celesti nutrire ire così grandi?
tr.es: ¿Caben tan grandes iras en los pechos celestiales?

notes.n: Arma virumque canō: canō 'I sing (of)' takes a direct object; -que joins virum to arma. canō has a frequentative cantō 'keep singing', which gave Italian cantare, Spanish cantar, French chanter.

Ītaliam … Lāvīniaque lītora: accusatives of motion towards without a preposition, a poetic licence (prose would use in or ad). The first syllable of Ītalia is lengthened to fit the hexameter. fātō profugus 'a fugitive by fate'.
et … et 'both … and'. altum, literally 'the deep', means 'the sea'. iactātus is from iactō, the frequentative of iaciō 'throw': 'thrown about again and again'.
superum is a short genitive plural for superōrum 'of the gods above', as deum for deōrum in line 9. memorem … īram: Juno's anger is 'mindful'—she never forgets an injury.
passus is the perfect participle of the deponent patior: 'having suffered'. dum + subjunctive (conderet, īnferret) means 'until he could found … and bring'.
Latiō is dative of direction, poetic for in Latium. unde '(from) where' here means 'from whom'. Latium → Italian Lazio; genus Latīnum → 'Latin', the name of the language itself.
quō nūmine laesō: an indirect question in the form of an ablative absolute, 'with what divine will (of hers) offended'. memorā, imperative of memorō 'recall, tell'.

quidve dolēns 'or grieving at what'; -ve means 'or'. deum = deōrum. volvere cāsūs 'to roll through disasters', as if life were a wheel or a scroll being unrolled. The infinitives volvere and adīre depend on impulerit.
pietās is Aeneas' defining virtue: dutiful devotion to the gods, to family and to country. Italian pietà and Spanish piedad have narrowed it to 'pity, piety'.

impulerit is perfect subjunctive, still in the indirect question after memorā. Tantaene animīs caelestibus īrae (sunt)?: -ne marks the question, animīs is a dative of possession and the verb is left out—'Do heavenly minds have such great angers?'

title: Daedalus and Icarus
author: Ovid
intro: Publius Ovidius Naso (43 BC–AD 17) retold some 250 myths of transformation in the fifteen books of the Metamorphoses. The inventor Daedalus, kept on Crete by King Minos, resolves to escape through the air; after a gap in which he builds the wings and warns his son, the excerpt resumes as young Icarus flies too close to the sun. The story has inspired painters from Bruegel to Matisse and poets from W. H. Auden to William Carlos Williams.

tr.en: Meanwhile Daedalus, hating Crete and his long
tr.it: Dedalo intanto, odiando Creta e il lungo
tr.es: Dédalo, entretanto, aborreciendo Creta y su largo

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. m. + -que

tr.en: exile, and moved by love for his native place,
tr.it: esilio, e toccato dall'amore per la terra natale,
tr.es: destierro, y movido por el amor a su tierra natal,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: was shut in by the sea. “He may block the lands,” he said, “and the waves,
tr.it: era chiuso dal mare. «Mi sbarri pure», disse, «le terre e le onde:
tr.es: estaba encerrado por el mar. «Que me cierre», dijo, «las tierras y las olas;

tr.en: but the sky at least lies open: we shall go that way.
tr.it: ma il cielo almeno è aperto: andremo per di là.
tr.es: pero el cielo, al menos, está abierto: iremos por allí.

tr.en: Though he owns everything, Minos does not own the air.”
tr.it: Possieda pure ogni cosa, Minosse non possiede l'aria».
tr.es: Aunque lo posea todo, Minos no posee el aire».

tr.en: …when the boy began to delight in his daring flight
tr.it: …quando il ragazzo cominciò a godere del volo audace
tr.es: …cuando el muchacho empezó a disfrutar del vuelo audaz

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: and left his guide, and, drawn by longing for the sky,
tr.it: e abbandonò la guida e, attratto dal desiderio del cielo,
tr.es: y abandonó a su guía y, arrastrado por el deseo del cielo,

tr.en: steered his course higher. The nearness of the scorching sun
tr.it: spinse più in alto il suo cammino. La vicinanza del sole divorante
tr.es: llevó más alto su camino. La cercanía del sol abrasador

tr.en: softens the fragrant wax that bound the feathers.
tr.it: ammorbidisce la cera profumata, legame delle penne.
tr.es: ablanda la cera olorosa, atadura de las plumas.

tr.en: The wax had melted: he shakes his bare arms,
tr.it: La cera si era sciolta: egli agita le braccia nude,
tr.es: La cera se había derretido: él agita los brazos desnudos,

tr.en: and, with no oars of feathers, he catches hold of no air,
tr.it: e, privo dei remi, non fa più presa sull'aria,
tr.es: y, sin sus remos, ya no logra asirse al aire,

tr.en: and his mouth, crying out his father's name,
tr.it: e la bocca, che gridava il nome del padre,
tr.es: y su boca, que gritaba el nombre de su padre,

tr.en: is swallowed by the dark-blue water, which took its name from him.
tr.it: è accolta dall'acqua azzurra, che da lui prese il nome.
tr.es: es tragada por el agua azul, que de él tomó su nombre.

tr.en: But the unhappy father, a father no longer, cried “Icarus!”,
tr.it: Ma il padre infelice, ormai non più padre, «Icaro», disse,
tr.es: Pero el desdichado padre, ya no padre, «¡Ícaro!», dijo,

tr.en: “Icarus,” he cried, “where are you? In what region am I to look for you?”
tr.it: «Icaro», disse, «dove sei? In quale regione devo cercarti?».
tr.es: «Ícaro», dijo, «¿dónde estás? ¿En qué región he de buscarte?».

tr.en: “Icarus,” he kept saying—then he saw the feathers on the waves,
tr.it: «Icaro» ripeteva: vide le penne sulle onde
tr.es: «Ícaro», repetía: vio las plumas sobre las olas

tr.en: and cursed his own skills, and laid the body
tr.it: e maledisse le sue arti, e compose il corpo
tr.es: y maldijo sus artes, y depositó el cuerpo

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.
perf. pass. ptcp. gen. sg. m.

tr.en: to rest in a tomb; and the land is called by the name of the one buried there.
tr.it: in un sepolcro; e la terra fu chiamata col nome del sepolto.
tr.es: en un sepulcro; y la tierra recibió el nombre del sepultado.

notes.n: Crētēn is a Greek accusative (Crētē, -ēs is Ovid's form of Crēta). perōsus 'utterly hating' (per + ōdī) is a participle with active meaning and governs both Crētēn and exsilium.
tāctus … amōre 'touched (moved) by love'. nātālis 'of birth' (from nātus) → Italian Natale, Portuguese Natal 'Christmas': the dies nātālis of Christ.
licet + subjunctive (obstruat) means 'granted that, although': 'he may block the lands and the waves, but …'. The subject is Minos, named only at the end of the speech.
ībimus is the future of eō 'go'. illāc 'by that way'. caelum → Italian and Spanish cielo, French ciel.
possideat is a concessive subjunctive: 'let him possess everything'. āera is the Greek accusative of āēr 'air' → Italian aria, Spanish aire, French air.

Here the excerpt skips some 35 lines: Daedalus builds the wings, warns his son to fly the middle course, and they set off past Samos and Delos. cum introduces the sudden turning point: 'when (all at once) the boy began…'.
altius is the comparative of the adverb altē 'high'. rapidus keeps its root sense 'seizing, devouring' (rapiō): the consuming heat of the sun.
pennārum vincula is in apposition to cērās: 'the wax, the bonds of the feathers'. penna → Italian penna 'feather, pen' (and the pasta penne); cēra → Italian and Spanish cera, French cire.
Tābuerant is pluperfect: the wax 'had (already) melted' before he noticed—Ovid jumps straight to the result. lacertus is the upper arm (compare lacerta 'lizard').
rēmigium 'oarage, set of oars': the wings are pictured as a ship's oars rowing through the air. careō takes the ablative: rēmigiō carēns 'lacking oars'.
ōra, plural for singular, 'mouth' (from ōs, ōris). clāmantia is a present participle agreeing with ōra. clāmāre gave Italian chiamare, Spanish llamar, Portuguese chamar 'to call'.
quae nōmen trāxit ab illō: the Icarian Sea, south-west of Samos, was named after him.
requīram is a deliberative subjunctive: 'where am I to look for you?'
dēvōvit 'cursed' (dēvoveō, literally 'vow away to the gods below'). sepulcrum → Italian sepolcro, Spanish sepulcro.
dicta (est): the island of Icaria. sepultī is the genitive of sepultus (sepeliō 'bury'), 'of the buried boy' → Italian sepolto, Spanish sepultado.

title: How Long, Catiline?
orig: Quō usque tandem abūtēre, Catilīna, patientiā nostrā?
author: Cicero
intro: On 8 November 63 BC the consul Marcus Tullius Cicero confronted the conspirator Lucius Sergius Catilina face to face in the Senate, which met that day under armed guard in the Temple of Jupiter Stator. The speech opens not with the usual courtesies but with a volley of furious questions. It became the model of Latin oratory, and 'Ō tempora, ō mōrēs!' is still quoted all over Europe.

tr.en: How long, Catiline, will you go on abusing our patience?
tr.it: Fino a quando, Catilina, abuserai della nostra pazienza?
tr.es: ¿Hasta cuándo, Catilina, abusarás de nuestra paciencia?

tr.en: How much longer will that madness of yours make fools of us?
tr.it: Per quanto tempo ancora codesta tua follia si farà beffe di noi?
tr.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo más se burlará de nosotros esa locura tuya?

tr.en: To what limit will your unbridled audacity flaunt itself?
tr.it: Fino a che punto si scatenerà la tua sfrenata audacia?
tr.es: ¿Hasta dónde llegará la jactancia de tu desenfrenada audacia?

tr.en: Has nothing moved you—not the night guard on the Palatine, not the patrols of the city, not the people's fear,
tr.it: Non ti hanno per nulla scosso il presidio notturno del Palatino, né le ronde della città, né la paura del popolo,
tr.es: ¿No te han conmovido en nada la guardia nocturna del Palatino, ni las rondas de la ciudad, ni el miedo del pueblo,

tr.en: not the gathering of all loyal citizens, not this most strongly fortified place for holding the Senate,
tr.it: né l'accorrere di tutti i buoni cittadini, né questo luogo fortificatissimo scelto per riunire il senato,
tr.es: ni la afluencia de todos los hombres de bien, ni este lugar tan fortificado para reunir al senado,

tr.en: not the faces and expressions of these men here?
tr.it: né i volti e gli sguardi di costoro?
tr.es: ni los rostros y las miradas de estos?

tr.en: Do you not realize that your plans are laid bare,
tr.it: Non ti accorgi che i tuoi piani sono scoperti,
tr.es: ¿No te das cuenta de que tus planes están al descubierto,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. acc. sg. f.

tr.en: do you not see that your conspiracy is already held fast, bound by the knowledge of all these men?
tr.it: non vedi che la tua congiura è ormai tenuta in pugno, nota a tutti costoro?
tr.es: no ves que tu conjura está ya atenazada por el conocimiento de todos estos?

tr.en: What you did last night, what the night before, where you were,
tr.it: Che cosa hai fatto la notte scorsa, che cosa quella precedente, dove sei stato,
tr.es: Qué hiciste la noche pasada, qué la anterior, dónde estuviste,

tr.en: whom you called together, what plan you made—which of us do you think does not know?
tr.it: chi hai convocato, quale decisione hai preso: chi di noi credi che lo ignori?
tr.es: a quiénes convocaste, qué decisión tomaste: ¿a quién de nosotros crees que se le oculta?

tr.en: Oh, the times! Oh, the morals!
tr.it: O tempi, o costumi!
tr.es: ¡Oh tiempos, oh costumbres!

tr.en: The Senate understands these things, the consul sees them; and yet this man lives.
tr.it: Il senato capisce queste cose, il console le vede; eppure costui vive.
tr.es: El senado comprende estas cosas, el cónsul las ve; y sin embargo este vive.

tr.en: Lives? Why, he even comes into the Senate, he takes part in the public council,
tr.it: Vive? Anzi, viene perfino in senato, prende parte alle decisioni pubbliche,
tr.es: ¿Vive? Más aún, incluso viene al senado, toma parte en el consejo público,

tr.en: he marks out and picks with his eyes every single one of us for slaughter.
tr.it: segna e designa con gli occhi, per la strage, ciascuno di noi.
tr.es: señala y marca con los ojos para la matanza a cada uno de nosotros.

tr.en: And we, brave men that we are, think we are doing our duty by the Republic
tr.it: E noi, uomini coraggiosi, crediamo di fare abbastanza per lo Stato
tr.es: Y nosotros, hombres valientes, creemos cumplir con la república

tr.en: if we dodge that man's frenzy and his weapons.
tr.it: se scansiamo il furore e le armi di costui.
tr.es: si esquivamos el furor y las armas de ese individuo.

tr.en: You ought long ago, Catiline, to have been led to execution on the consul's orders,
tr.it: Già da tempo, Catilina, avresti dovuto essere condotto a morte per ordine del console,
tr.es: Hace ya tiempo, Catilina, que deberías haber sido llevado a la muerte por orden del cónsul,

tr.en: and the ruin you have long been plotting against us all should have been turned on you.
tr.it: e su di te doveva ricadere la rovina che tu da tempo trami contro tutti noi.
tr.es: y sobre ti debería haber recaído la ruina que tú desde hace tiempo maquinas contra todos nosotros.

notes.n: abūtēre is the alternative form of abūtēris, 2nd singular future of the deponent abūtor 'use up, abuse', which takes the ablative (patientiā nostrā). tandem in questions shows impatience: 'how long, pray?'. patientia → Italian pazienza, Spanish paciencia, French patience.
iste 'that … of yours' often sounds contemptuous in speeches. ēlūdet: future of ēlūdō 'make sport of, mock' (ex + lūdō 'play').
Quem ad fīnem 'to what end, how far?'. sēsē is an emphatic sē. effrēnātus 'unbridled' (ex + frēnum 'bridle') → Italian sfrenato, Spanish desenfrenado.

Six nihil's in a row (anaphora) hammer the point; nihil is used adverbially, 'not at all', and -ne turns the whole sentence into a question. Palātī is the old genitive in -ī of Palātium, the Palatine hill—later the emperors' residence, hence palace, Italian palazzo, French palais.
habendī senātūs: gerundive in the genitive, 'of holding the Senate'. bonī 'the good' means the loyal, conservative citizens.

Patēre … sentīs: accusative and infinitive after a verb of perceiving, 'you feel (that) your plans lie open'. cōnsilium means 'plan, deliberation, council' → Italian consiglio, Spanish consejo 'advice'.
ēgeris, fueris, convocāveris, cēperis are perfect subjunctives in indirect questions, all depending on ignōrāre in the next line. proximā (nocte) 'last night', superiōre nocte 'the night before'.
quem nostrum 'which of us': nostrum is the partitive genitive of nōs (compare nostrī, the objective genitive). arbitrāris is a deponent, 'you think'.
The most famous exclamation in Latin oratory, in the accusative of exclamation. tempus → Italian tempo, Spanish tiempo, French temps; mōs, mōris 'custom' gave mōrālis, English moral.
Immō vērō 'no indeed, rather': a self-correction that goes further. particeps (pars + capiō) 'sharing in' → participate.

satis facere 'to do enough' → satisfacere, English satisfy, Italian soddisfare, Spanish satisfacer. reī pūblicae is the dative of rēs pūblica 'the commonwealth', whence republic, Italian repubblica. vidēmur 'we seem (to ourselves)', bitterly ironic.
oportēbat + accusative and infinitive (tē dūcī) in the past tense expresses what should have happened but did not: 'you ought to have been led'. iussū 'by order' occurs only in the ablative.
māchināris (deponent) 'you are contriving', from māchina 'device', from Greek μηχανή → machine. With iam diū the present means 'have long been plotting'.

title: Our Heart Is Restless
author: Augustine of Hippo
intro: Aurelius Augustinus (AD 354–430), bishop of Hippo in North Africa, wrote the Confessions as one long prayer addressed to God, telling the story of his restless youth and his conversion. The opening paragraph weaves quotations from the Psalms and the New Testament into rhetoric learned in the classical schools. Its sentence about the restless heart is among the most quoted in Christian literature.

tr.en: You are great, Lord, and greatly to be praised:
tr.it: Grande sei, Signore, e degno di ogni lode:
tr.es: Grande eres, Señor, y muy digno de alabanza:

tr.en: great is your power, and your wisdom is beyond measure.
tr.it: grande è la tua potenza, e la tua sapienza non ha misura.
tr.es: grande es tu poder, y tu sabiduría no tiene medida.

tr.en: And man wants to praise you, man, some small part of your creation,
tr.it: E l'uomo vuole lodarti, l'uomo, una piccola parte della tua creazione,
tr.es: Y el hombre quiere alabarte, el hombre, una pequeña parte de tu creación,

tr.en: man who carries his mortality about with him,
tr.it: un uomo che porta con sé la propria mortalità,
tr.es: un hombre que lleva consigo su mortalidad,

tr.en: carries about the evidence of his sin
tr.it: che porta con sé la testimonianza del suo peccato
tr.es: que lleva consigo el testimonio de su pecado

tr.en: and the evidence that you resist the proud;
tr.it: e la testimonianza che tu resisti ai superbi;
tr.es: y el testimonio de que tú resistes a los soberbios;

tr.en: and yet man wants to praise you, some small part of your creation.
tr.it: eppure l'uomo vuole lodarti, una piccola parte della tua creazione.
tr.es: y, sin embargo, el hombre quiere alabarte, una pequeña parte de tu creación.

tr.en: You stir him up, so that to praise you is his delight,
tr.it: Sei tu che lo spingi a trovare gioia nel lodarti,
tr.es: Tú lo mueves a que se deleite en alabarte,

tr.en: because you made us for yourself, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.
tr.it: perché ci hai fatti per te, e il nostro cuore è inquieto finché non riposa in te.
tr.es: porque nos hiciste para ti, y nuestro corazón está inquieto hasta que descanse en ti.

tr.en: Grant me, Lord, to know and understand
tr.it: Concedimi, Signore, di sapere e di capire
tr.es: Concédeme, Señor, saber y entender

tr.en: whether calling upon you comes first, or praising you,
tr.it: se venga prima invocarti o lodarti,
tr.es: si es primero invocarte o alabarte,

tr.en: and whether knowing you comes first, or calling upon you.
tr.it: e se venga prima conoscerti o invocarti.
tr.es: y si es primero conocerte o invocarte.

notes.n: Augustine opens with the words of the Psalms (Psalm 145:3 and 147:5 in modern numbering). valdē 'very' is a contraction of validē 'strongly'. laudābilis 'praiseworthy' → Italian lodevole, Spanish loable; the suffix -bilis gave English -able/-ible.
sapientiae tuae nōn est numerus is a dative of possession, 'your wisdom has no number', copying the Hebrew idiom 'to his understanding there is no number'. virtūs here means 'power', not 'virtue'.

vult is from volō 'want', with its irregular present (volō, vīs, vult). aliqua portiō creātūrae tuae stands in apposition to homō: 'a fragment of your creation'. portiō → Italian porzione, Spanish porción, English portion.
circumferēns 'carrying around' (circum + ferō) is a present participle. mortālitās is the state of being mortal—in Augustine's theology, the consequence of sin.

quia superbīs resistis echoes 1 Peter 5:5 and James 4:6 ('God resists the proud'). quia, normally 'because', here introduces the content of the testimony, 'that'—a Late Latin use that foreshadows Romance che, que.
excitās 'you rouse' → excite. ut … dēlectet: a clause of purpose or result with dēlectat 'it delights' used impersonally: 'so that praising you delights (him)'.

fēcistī nōs ad tē: ad expresses direction and goal, 'towards you, for you'. dōnec + subjunctive 'until'. cor → Italian cuore, French cœur; Spanish corazón and Portuguese coração come from an enlarged form *corātiōnem. inquiētus → Italian and Spanish inquieto.
Dā mihi … scīre 'grant me to know': dō with an infinitive is a poetic and late construction.

utrum … an 'whether … or' introduces a double indirect question, so sit is subjunctive. prius 'earlier, prior' is the neuter of prior, used predicatively with the infinitives as subjects. invocāre → invoke, Italian invocare.

title: Pyramus and Thisbe
author: Ovid
intro: In Book 4 of the Metamorphoses the daughters of Minyas pass the time at their looms by telling stories, and this is the first. Two young neighbours in Babylon, forbidden by their fathers to marry, talk through a crack in the wall between their houses; the tale will end in a double suicide under a mulberry tree, whose fruit turns dark red. Shakespeare used it twice: as the plot behind Romeo and Juliet, and as the play the workmen perform in A Midsummer Night's Dream, where 'Wall' becomes a character.

tr.en: Pyramus and Thisbe—he the most handsome of young men,
tr.it: Piramo e Tisbe, l'uno il più bello dei giovani,
tr.es: Píramo y Tisbe, él el más hermoso de los jóvenes,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: she preferred above all the girls the East possessed—
tr.it: l'altra preferita a tutte le fanciulle che ebbe l'Oriente,
tr.es: ella preferida a todas las muchachas que tuvo el Oriente,

tr.en: lived in neighbouring houses, where Semiramis is said
tr.it: abitavano case vicine, là dove si dice che Semiramide
tr.es: habitaban casas contiguas, allí donde se dice que Semíramis

tr.en: to have girded her lofty city with walls of baked brick.
tr.it: abbia cinto l'alta città di mura di mattoni.
tr.es: ciñó su alta ciudad con murallas de ladrillo.

tr.en: Being neighbours brought acquaintance and the first steps;
tr.it: La vicinanza fece nascere la conoscenza e i primi passi;
tr.es: La vecindad trajo el trato y los primeros pasos;

tr.en: with time love grew; they would have joined, too, by right of the marriage torch,
tr.it: col tempo crebbe l'amore; si sarebbero anche uniti col diritto della fiaccola nuziale,
tr.es: con el tiempo creció el amor; se habrían unido también por derecho de la antorcha nupcial,

tr.en: but their fathers forbade it; what they could not forbid:
tr.it: ma i padri lo vietarono; ciò che non poterono vietare:
tr.es: pero sus padres lo prohibieron; lo que no pudieron prohibir:

w: perf. pass. ptcp. abl. pl. f.

tr.en: both burned equally, their hearts held captive.
tr.it: ardevano entrambi allo stesso modo, con i cuori prigionieri.
tr.es: ambos ardían por igual, con los corazones cautivos.

tr.en: No one shares their secret; they talk by nods and signs,
tr.it: Non c'è alcun confidente; parlano con cenni e segni,
tr.es: No hay ningún confidente; hablan con gestos y señas,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: and the more the fire is covered, the more fiercely, covered, it blazes.
tr.it: e quanto più è coperto, tanto più, coperto, divampa il fuoco.
tr.es: y cuanto más se cubre, más arde, cubierto, el fuego.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: Split by a thin crack, which it had formed long ago
tr.it: Era spaccata da una sottile fessura, che si era formata un tempo,
tr.es: Estaba hendida por una fina grieta, que se le había abierto antaño,

tr.en: while it was being built, was the wall shared by the two houses.
tr.it: quando la si costruiva, la parete comune alle due case.
tr.es: cuando la construían, la pared común a las dos casas.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. n.

tr.en: That flaw, noticed by no one through long ages—
tr.it: Quel difetto, da nessuno notato per lunghi secoli—
tr.es: Ese defecto, que nadie había advertido durante largos siglos—

tr.en: what does love not notice?—you, lovers, were the first to see,
tr.it: che cosa non avverte l'amore?—voi, amanti, per primi lo vedeste
tr.es: ¿qué no percibe el amor?—vosotros, amantes, fuisteis los primeros en verlo

tr.en: and you made it a path for your voices; and safely through it
tr.it: e ne faceste un passaggio per la voce; e sicure attraverso di esso
tr.es: y lo hicisteis camino de la voz; y seguras a través de él

tr.en: your sweet words used to pass in the faintest whisper.
tr.it: le vostre tenerezze passavano in un sussurro lievissimo.
tr.es: vuestras ternuras solían pasar en un murmullo levísimo.

notes.n: alter … altera 'the one … the other'. pulcherrimus is the superlative of pulcher, with the partitive genitive iuvenum 'of the young men'.
quās Oriēns habuit: the relative clause comes before its antecedent puellīs. praelāta 'preferred, ranked before' is the participle of praeferō and takes a dative.
tenuēre = tenuērunt: -ēre is a common poetic alternative ending for the 3rd plural perfect. dīcitur … cīnxisse 'is said to have girded': a personal passive with the perfect infinitive.
coctilibus mūrīs: walls of baked brick, as Herodotus describes Babylon's. Semiramis was the legendary queen of Babylon. mūrus → Italian and Spanish muro, French mur.
vīcīnia 'neighbourhood' is from vīcīnus 'neighbour' (vīcus 'village') → Italian vicino, Spanish vecino, French voisin.

taedae iūre 'by right of the torch': the bride was escorted to her new home by torchlight, so taeda can stand for 'marriage'. coīssent (= coīvissent, from coeō 'come together') is a pluperfect subjunctive in an unreal condition: 'they would have married'.
vetuēre … vetāre: Ovid plays on the same verb vetō 'forbid'. quod nōn potuēre vetāre sums up the next line: the one thing the fathers could not forbid was that both should burn with love.
ex aequō 'equally'. captīs … mentibus is an ablative absolute, 'their minds captured'. ambō 'both' → Spanish and Portuguese ambos; Italian entrambi (inter ambōs).
cōnscius 'one who knows with (them)', a confidant. nūtus 'nod' is from nuō 'nod'.
quō magis … magis 'the more … the more': quō is ablative of degree of difference. ignis was replaced in Romance by focus 'hearth': Italian fuoco, Spanish fuego, French feu.
fissus erat … pariēs: the subject arrives only at the end of the next line. dūxerat 'had drawn, developed'. rīma 'crack' is the opposite of the lovers' secret: an opening.

cum fieret: imperfect subjunctive of fīō, 'when it was being made'. pariēs is a house wall (mūrus a city wall) → Italian parete, Spanish pared, French paroi. utrīque is the dative of uterque 'each of two'.
The poet turns and speaks to the lovers directly (apostrophe): vīdistis 'you saw', amantēs vocative plural of the participle, 'you lovers'.
blanditiae 'caresses, sweet words' → Italian blandizie, English blandishments. murmure minimō 'in the faintest murmur'. solēbant 'they used to' marks a repeated habit.

title: Seize the Day
author: Horace
intro: Quintus Horatius Flaccus (65–8 BC) addresses this eight-line ode to a woman called Leuconoe, who has been consulting astrologers about how long she and the poet will live. His answer, in the long 'greater Asclepiad' metre, is to stop asking, strain the wine and live today. Its last line gave the world the phrase carpe diem.

tr.en: Do not ask—to know is forbidden—what end for me, what end for you
tr.it: Tu non chiedere—saperlo non è lecito—quale fine a me, quale a te
tr.es: Tú no preguntes—saberlo no está permitido—qué fin a mí, qué fin a ti

tr.en: the gods have given, Leuconoe, and do not meddle with Babylonian
tr.it: abbiano dato gli dèi, Leuconoe, e non tentare i calcoli
tr.es: han dado los dioses, Leucónoe, y no consultes los cálculos

tr.en: calculations. How much better to endure whatever will be!
tr.it: babilonesi. Quanto è meglio sopportare qualunque cosa sarà!
tr.es: babilónicos. ¡Cuánto mejor es soportar lo que haya de ser!

tr.en: Whether Jupiter has granted us more winters, or this one as our last,
tr.it: Sia che Giove ci abbia assegnato altri inverni, sia che questo sia l'ultimo,
tr.es: Tanto si Júpiter nos ha concedido más inviernos como si este es el último,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. abl. pl. m.

tr.en: which now wears out the sea against the facing cliffs of pumice—
tr.it: che ora sfianca contro gli scogli di pomice che gli stanno di fronte il mare
tr.es: que ahora quebranta contra los peñascos de piedra pómez el mar

tr.en: the Tyrrhenian: be wise, strain the wine, and, since life's span is short,
tr.it: Tirreno: sii saggia, filtra il vino, e poiché lo spazio è breve
tr.es: Tirreno: sé sensata, filtra el vino y, puesto que el plazo es breve,

tr.en: cut back long hope. Even as we speak, envious time
tr.it: recidi la lunga speranza. Mentre parliamo, sarà già fuggito il tempo
tr.es: poda la larga esperanza. Mientras hablamos, habrá huido el tiempo

tr.en: will have fled: seize the day, trusting as little as possible in tomorrow.
tr.it: invidioso: cogli il giorno, fidandoti il meno possibile del domani.
tr.es: envidioso: aprovecha el día, confiando lo menos posible en el mañana.

notes.n: nē + perfect subjunctive (quaesierīs) is the normal Latin prohibition: 'don't ask'. scīre nefās (est) is a parenthesis: 'to know is forbidden (by divine law)'. nefās is indeclinable.
dederint is perfect subjunctive in an indirect question. Babylōniōs numerōs: the astrologers' tables for casting horoscopes—'Chaldaean' astrology was the fashion in Rome.

temptāris is the contracted form of temptāverīs (perfect subjunctive), still governed by nē … nec. Ut melius: exclamatory ut, 'how much better!'. patī is the infinitive of the deponent patior 'suffer, endure' → English patient, Italian paziente.

seu … seu 'whether … or'. plūrīs is the older spelling of the accusative plural plūrēs (also in omnīs, fīnīs). Horace counts life in winters. hiems was replaced in Romance by (tempus) hībernum: Italian inverno, Spanish invierno, French hiver, Portuguese inverno.

pūmicibus: the porous volcanic rocks of the coast near Naples. The winter storm 'weakens' the sea by breaking it on the cliffs—an image of time grinding everything down. oppositīs agrees with pūmicibus.
sapiās, liquēs, resecēs are jussive subjunctives, gentler than imperatives. vīna liquēs: wine was strained through cloth before drinking. spatium → Italian spazio, Spanish espacio, French espace.
fūgerit is future perfect: by the time we finish speaking, time 'will already have fled'. invida 'envious' agrees with aetās at the start of the next line; aetās → Italian età, Spanish edad.

carpe is the imperative of carpō 'pluck, pick': the day is to be picked like ripe fruit. quam minimum 'as little as possible'. crēdula agrees with Leuconoe; posterō (diēī) 'the next day'. diēs → Spanish día, while Italian giorno and French jour come from diurnum.

title: The Cloud over Vesuvius
orig: Erat Mīsēnī classemque imperiō praesēns regēbat
author: Pliny the Younger
intro: Gaius Plinius Caecilius Secundus was seventeen when Vesuvius erupted in AD 79. His uncle, the naturalist Pliny the Elder, commanded the Roman fleet at Misenum across the Bay of Naples and died trying to rescue people trapped on the coast. Years later the historian Tacitus asked for an account, and Pliny wrote this letter; his description of the eruption column, spreading like an umbrella pine, is so exact that volcanologists still call this type of eruption 'Plinian'.

tr.en: He was at Misenum, commanding the fleet in person.
tr.it: Si trovava a Miseno e comandava di persona la flotta.
tr.es: Estaba en Miseno y mandaba la flota en persona.

tr.en: On the ninth day before the Kalends of September, at about the seventh hour, my mother points out to him
tr.it: Il nono giorno prima delle calende di settembre, verso l'ora settima, mia madre gli fa notare
tr.es: El noveno día antes de las calendas de septiembre, hacia la hora séptima, mi madre le señala

tr.en: that a cloud of unusual size and appearance is coming into view.
tr.it: che sta comparendo una nube insolita per grandezza e per aspetto.
tr.es: que está apareciendo una nube insólita tanto por su tamaño como por su aspecto.

tr.en: He had taken the sun, then a cold bath, had eaten a light lunch lying down, and was working at his books;
tr.it: Egli aveva preso il sole, poi un bagno freddo, aveva fatto uno spuntino sdraiato e stava studiando;
tr.es: Él había tomado el sol y luego un baño frío, había comido algo recostado y estaba estudiando;

tr.en: he calls for his sandals and climbs to a spot from which that marvel could best be seen.
tr.it: chiede i sandali e sale in un punto da cui si poteva vedere meglio quel prodigio.
tr.es: pide las sandalias y sube a un lugar desde el que mejor se podía contemplar aquel prodigio.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. n.

tr.en: A cloud—to people watching from far away it was unclear from which mountain (it was later known to be Vesuvius)—was rising,
tr.it: Una nube—per chi guardava da lontano non era chiaro da quale monte (si seppe poi che era il Vesuvio)—si stava levando,
tr.es: Una nube—para quienes miraban de lejos no estaba claro de qué monte (luego se supo que era el Vesubio)—se estaba alzando,

tr.en: whose look and shape no tree would capture better than a pine.
tr.it: il cui aspetto e la cui forma nessun albero renderebbe meglio di un pino.
tr.es: cuyo aspecto y forma ningún árbol reproduciría mejor que un pino.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: For it was carried up high on what looked like a very tall trunk and then spread out into a kind of branches,
tr.it: Infatti, innalzatasi come su un altissimo tronco, si allargava in una specie di rami,
tr.es: Pues, elevada como sobre un tronco altísimo, se desplegaba en una especie de ramas,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.
perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: because, I believe, it was lifted by a fresh blast and then, as that blast weakened, was left without support,
tr.it: credo perché sollevata da un soffio recente e poi, quando questo si affievoliva, rimasta senza sostegno,
tr.es: creo que porque fue alzada por un soplo reciente y luego, al debilitarse este, quedó sin sostén,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: or else, overcome by its own weight, it thinned out sideways,
tr.it: o anche vinta dal proprio peso, si dissolveva in larghezza,
tr.es: o también vencida por su propio peso, se desvanecía a lo ancho,

tr.en: white at times, at times dirty and blotched, depending on whether it had carried up earth or ash.
tr.it: a volte bianca, a volte sporca e chiazzata, a seconda che avesse sollevato terra o cenere.
tr.es: unas veces blanca, otras sucia y manchada, según hubiera levantado tierra o ceniza.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. n.

tr.en: To a man of his great learning it seemed important and worth a closer look.
tr.it: A un uomo di grande cultura come lui parve un fenomeno importante, da conoscere più da vicino.
tr.es: A un hombre tan erudito le pareció algo importante y digno de conocerse más de cerca.

tr.en: He orders a fast galley to be made ready; he offers me the chance to come along, if I wished;
tr.it: Ordina di preparare una liburna; a me offre di venire con lui, se volevo;
tr.es: Manda preparar una libúrnica; a mí me ofrece la posibilidad de acompañarlo, si quería;

tr.en: I replied that I would rather study, and as it happened he himself had given me something to write.
tr.it: risposi che preferivo studiare, e per caso proprio lui mi aveva dato qualcosa da scrivere.
tr.es: le respondí que prefería estudiar, y precisamente él mismo me había dado algo que escribir.

notes.n: Mīsēnī is locative, 'at Misenum', the naval base at the north-west tip of the Bay of Naples. praesēns 'present, in person'; imperiō is ablative of means, 'with full authority'.

Nōnum Kal. Septembrēs is short for ante diem nōnum Kalendās Septembrēs; counting inclusively, 24 August. Roman hours ran from sunrise, so the seventh hour is just after noon. Notice the historic presents (indicat, poscit, ascendit), which make the story vivid.

appārēre (ad + pāreō 'appear') → Italian apparire, Spanish aparecer, French apparaître. nūbēs → Spanish nube, Portuguese nuvem; Italian prefers nuvola (from nūbila) and French nuage (from a derivative).

Ūsus … sōle, mox frīgidā (aquā): ūtor takes the ablative, 'having used the sun, then cold (water)'—a sunbath followed by a cold bath, part of a Roman gentleman's routine. gustāverat 'he had had a bite to eat' (gustō 'taste' → Italian gustare, Spanish gustar).
maximē, the superlative adverb 'most of all', here 'best'. cōnspicī is a present passive infinitive. mīrāculum 'a wonder' (mīror 'marvel at') → Italian miracolo, Spanish milagro, French miracle.

incertum (erat) procul intuentibus: a dative of reference, 'it was uncertain to those looking from afar'. The parenthesis is Pliny writing with hindsight. Vesuvium fuisse … cognitum est: accusative and infinitive after an impersonal passive.

expresserit is a potential subjunctive: 'no tree would express it better'. Pliny means the Mediterranean umbrella pine, with a tall bare trunk and a flat spreading crown. pīnus → Italian pino, Spanish pino, French pin.
ēlāta is the perfect participle of efferō 'carry out, lift up' (ex + ferō, stem lāt-). in altum 'into the height', i.e. upwards.
crēdō 'I believe' is inserted as Pliny offers a scientific explanation. senēscente eō is an ablative absolute: 'as it (the blast) grew old', i.e. weakened.
prout 'according as'. sustulerat is the pluperfect of tollō 'lift' (tollō, tollere, sustulī, sublātum). cinis → Italian cenere, French cendre, Spanish ceniza.
Magnum … nōscendum (vīsum est): nōscendum is a gerundive of obligation, 'to be investigated'. ut 'as (befitted)' a very learned man: the uncle was the author of the 37-book Natural History.

Liburnica (nāvis) was a light, fast galley, named after the Liburnian seafarers of the Adriatic. facit cōpiam 'gives the opportunity'. vellem is subjunctive because the condition belongs to the uncle's offer as reported.
mālle 'to prefer' (magis + velle). quod scrīberem 'something to write' is a relative clause of purpose. This choice saved young Pliny's life: his uncle never came back.

title: Dikaiopolis the Farmer
author: Stemma
intro: Our first reading follows Dikaiopolis ('Just-City'), a farmer in the Attic countryside; the name is borrowed from the hero of Aristophanes' comedy Acharnians (425 BC), who longs for his village and for peace. Everything is in the present tense, and almost every noun belongs to the 1st or 2nd declension. Watch the article (ὁ, ἡ, τό): it tells you gender, number and case at a glance.

tr.en: Dikaiopolis is a farmer and lives in a small village in Attica.
tr.el: Ο Δικαιόπολις είναι γεωργός και μένει σε ένα μικρό χωριό της Αττικής.

tr.en: The house is small, but the field is beautiful.
tr.el: Το σπίτι είναι μικρό, το χωράφι όμως είναι όμορφο.

tr.en: In the field there are olive trees and vines.
tr.el: Στο χωράφι υπάρχουν ελιές και αμπέλια.

tr.en: Every day Dikaiopolis works hard in the field, for he loves the field.
tr.el: Κάθε μέρα ο Δικαιόπολις κοπιάζει στο χωράφι· γιατί αγαπά το χωράφι του.

tr.en: His wife, Philinna, stays in the house and weaves.
tr.el: Η γυναίκα του, η Φιλίννα, μένει στο σπίτι και υφαίνει.
