tr.en: His son, Theodoros, leads the sheep to the hill.
tr.el: Ο γιος του, ο Θεόδωρος, οδηγεί τα πρόβατα στον λόφο.

tr.en: His daughter, Eirene, carries the water jar from the spring.
tr.el: Η κόρη του, η Ειρήνη, φέρνει τη στάμνα από την πηγή.

tr.en: It is midday, and the sun is shining.
tr.el: Είναι μεσημέρι και ο ήλιος λάμπει.

tr.en: Dikaiopolis is tired and sleeps under the olive tree.
tr.el: Ο Δικαιόπολις κουράζεται και κοιμάται κάτω από την ελιά.

tr.en: It is already evening, and Dikaiopolis walks home.
tr.el: Είναι πια βράδυ, και ο Δικαιόπολις γυρίζει με τα πόδια στο σπίτι.

tr.en: Philinna serves dinner: bread and cheese and olives and wine.
tr.el: Η Φιλίννα σερβίρει το δείπνο: ψωμί, τυρί, ελιές και κρασί.

tr.en: So they eat and drink and are happy.
tr.el: Τρώνε λοιπόν, πίνουν και χαίρονται.

tr.en: For life in the countryside is hard, but beautiful.
tr.el: Γιατί η ζωή στην εξοχή είναι δύσκολη, αλλά όμορφη.

notes.n: γεωργός 'farmer' = γῆ 'earth' + ἔργον 'work': hence the name George and Virgil's Georgics. Modern Greek still says γεωργός, γεωργία 'agriculture'.
ἐστιν is an enclitic: it leans on the word before and normally loses its own accent. That is why γεωργός keeps its acute instead of turning grave.
μέν … δέ balances two ideas, 'on the one hand … on the other'; usually just 'but' in English. ὁ δὲ ἀγρὸς καλός has no verb: ἐστί is understood, a very common Greek habit.

ἄμπελος 'vine' is 2nd declension like λόγος but feminine, as names of trees usually are (ἡ ἄμπελος). Modern αμπέλι 'vineyard' comes from the diminutive ἀμπέλιον. ἐλαία 'olive (tree)' → Modern ελιά, Latin olīva, English olive.
Καθ’ ἡμέραν: κατά loses its final vowel (elision) and τ becomes θ before the rough breathing of ἡμέραν. Modern Greek has καθημερινός 'daily' and the newspaper Καθημερινή.
ὑφαίνω 'weave' → Modern υφαίνω, ύφασμα 'fabric'.

θυγάτηρ is a cousin of English daughter and German Tochter. Modern Greek replaced it with κόρη (Ancient κόρη 'girl', as in the Acropolis Korai). κρήνη 'spring, fountain' → Modern κρήνη (a public fountain).
μεσημβρία 'midday' = μέσος 'middle' + ἡμέρα 'day' → Modern μεσημέρι. Latin built the same idea: merīdiēs < medius diēs, whence meridian.
κάμνω 'toil, be weary'. ὑπό + dative = 'under' (place where).
ἑσπέρα 'evening' is cognate with Latin vesper (vespers, Italian vespro); Modern Greek keeps it in εσπερινός 'evening service'. οἴκαδε 'homewards': -δε marks motion towards.

ἄρτος 'bread' is replaced in Modern Greek by ψωμί (ψωμίον 'morsel'), but survives in church. οἶνος became κρασί, from κρᾶσις 'mixing', because wine was drunk mixed with water; οἶνος and Latin vīnum are related. τυρός → Modern τυρί; βού-τυρον 'cow-cheese' gave English butter.
The 3rd person plural ends in -ουσι(ν); the 'movable ν' appears before a vowel or a pause. Modern Greek τρώνε, πίνουν continue the same ending (-ουσι → -ουν).
βίος 'life, livelihood' → biology, biography. Modern Greek says ζωή for 'life' and keeps βίος for 'way of life, living'.

title: Greek Maxims
author: Various
source: Delphic maxims, the Seven Sages, Heraclitus, Socrates, Protagoras, Hippocrates, proverbs
intro: Short sayings were the Greeks' portable wisdom. Three were carved at the entrance to Apollo's temple at Delphi; others were credited to the 'Seven Sages' of the 6th century BC or to thinkers such as Heraclitus, Socrates and Protagoras. Many have no verb (ἐστί is understood), and many live on in Latin translation and in Modern Greek speech.

tr.en: Know yourself.
tr.el: Γνώρισε τον εαυτό σου.

tr.en: Nothing in excess.
tr.el: Τίποτα σε υπερβολή.

tr.en: Give a pledge, and ruin is at hand.
tr.el: Εγγύηση, και η καταστροφή είναι κοντά.

tr.en: Everything flows.
tr.el: Όλα ρέουν.

tr.en: Fine things are hard.
tr.el: Τα ωραία είναι δύσκολα.

tr.en: One thing I know: that I know nothing.
tr.el: Ένα πράγμα ξέρω, ότι δεν ξέρω τίποτα.

tr.en: Man is the measure of all things.
tr.el: Ο άνθρωπος είναι το μέτρο όλων των πραγμάτων.

tr.en: Life is short, but art is long.
tr.el: Η ζωή είναι σύντομη, ενώ η τέχνη μακρόχρονη.

tr.en: The beginning is half of the whole.
tr.el: Η αρχή είναι το ήμισυ του παντός.

tr.en: Moderation is best.
tr.el: Το μέτρο είναι το καλύτερο.

tr.en: Know the right moment.
tr.el: Να ξέρεις ποια είναι η κατάλληλη στιγμή.

tr.en: Practice is everything.
tr.el: Η άσκηση είναι το παν.

tr.en: Most people are bad.
tr.el: Οι περισσότεροι άνθρωποι είναι κακοί.

tr.en: Friends share everything.
tr.el: Οι φίλοι τα έχουν όλα κοινά.

tr.en: In wine there is truth.
tr.el: Στο κρασί βρίσκεται η αλήθεια.

tr.en: Make haste slowly.
tr.el: Βιάσου αργά.

notes.n: Inscribed in the forecourt of Apollo's temple at Delphi; Latin nōsce tē ipsum. γνῶθι is the root aorist imperative of γιγνώσκω, cognate with Latin (g)nōscō and English know; gnosis and diagnosis share the root. σεαυτόν = σέ + αὐτόν 'yourself'.
Also from Delphi; Latin nē quid nimis. μηδέν 'nothing' uses μή, the negative of commands; ἄγαν 'too much'.

The third Delphic maxim, in Doric dialect (Attic ἐγγύη, ἄτη): 'a pledge, and ruin is near' — warning against standing surety for others. πάρα, with the accent thrown back, stands for πάρεστι 'is present'. Ἄτη 'ruin, blind folly' was also a goddess. ἐγγύη → Modern εγγύηση 'guarantee'.

The ancient summary (in Simplicius) of Heraclitus' teaching that everything is in flux (c. 500 BC); compare his 'you cannot step twice into the same river'. ῥέω 'flow' → Modern ρέω, ρεύμα 'current, electricity'; English rheumatism, diarrhoea.

A proverb Socrates quotes in Plato (Republic 435c, Hippias Major 304e). Neuter plural adjectives used as nouns: τὰ καλά 'beautiful/noble things'. Note the neuter plural subject with no verb: ἐστί is understood.
A traditional summary of Socrates' words in Plato's Apology (21d); the exact phrase is not in Plato. οἶδα is a perfect with present meaning 'I know'. Modern Greek says ξέρω (from ἐξεύρω 'find out').

The opening of Protagoras' treatise 'Truth' (5th c. BC), quoted by Plato (Theaetetus 152a) and Sextus Empiricus; it continues 'of things that are, that they are, and of things that are not, that they are not'. χρῆμα 'thing', plural 'money' → Modern χρήματα 'money'. μέτρον → metre.

The first aphorism of Hippocrates (5th c. BC), in Ionic dialect: μακρή for Attic μακρά. Through Seneca's Latin it became ars longa, vīta brevis. τέχνη 'craft, skill' (here medicine) → technique, technology; βραχύς is cognate with Latin brevis.

A proverb quoted by Plato (Laws 753e) and Aristotle. Modern Greeks still say it in this very form, 'Η αρχή είναι το ήμισυ του παντός'. ἥμισυς 'half' is cognate with Latin sēmi-: hemisphere / semicircle.
Saying of Cleobulus of Lindos, one of the Seven Sages. μέτρον here means 'due measure'. ἄριστος 'best' is the superlative of ἀγαθός → aristocracy.
Saying of Pittacus of Mytilene. καιρός is the 'right moment, opportunity', as opposed to χρόνος 'time'. In Modern Greek καιρός means both 'time' and 'weather'.
Saying of Periander of Corinth. μελέτη 'care, practice' → Modern μελέτη 'study'.
Saying of Bias of Priene. πλεῖστος 'most' is the superlative of πολύς (Pleistocene 'most recent'). κακός 'bad' → cacophony; Modern κακός.

A Pythagorean proverb quoted by Plato (Phaedrus 279c) and Aristotle; Erasmus put its Latin form, amīcōrum omnia commūnia, first in his Adages. τὰ τῶν φίλων 'the things of friends': the article turns a genitive into a noun phrase.
A Greek proverb going back to the poet Alcaeus; Latin in vīnō vēritās. ἀλήθεια 'truth', literally 'not-escaping-notice' (ἀ- + λήθ-), → Modern αλήθεια.
The favourite saying of the emperor Augustus, according to Suetonius (Augustus 25); Latin festīnā lentē. σπεῦδε is a present imperative ('keep hurrying'). βραδύς 'slow' → bradycardia.

title: To Athens
author: Stemma
intro: Dikaiopolis and his son take their olive oil to market in Athens. The agora was the city's market place and civic centre; above it rose the Acropolis with the Parthenon, the temple of Athena Parthenos, completed in 432 BC. Still all present tense; new are contract verbs (ὁρᾷ, τιμῶσι) and the vocative (ὦ πάτερ).

tr.en: Dikaiopolis and Theodoros are walking to Athens.
tr.el: Ο Δικαιόπολις και ο Θεόδωρος περπατούν προς την Αθήνα.

tr.en: The donkey walks slowly and carries the olive oil.
tr.el: Ο γάιδαρος περπατά αργά και κουβαλά το λάδι.

tr.en: The road is long, but Theodoros does not get tired.
tr.el: Ο δρόμος είναι μακρύς, αλλά ο Θεόδωρος δεν κουράζεται.

tr.en: When they reach the city, they hurry to the agora.
tr.el: Όταν φτάνουν στην πόλη, πηγαίνουν βιαστικά στην αγορά.

tr.en: In the agora there are many people, both citizens and foreigners.
tr.el: Στην αγορά υπάρχουν πολλοί άνθρωποι, και πολίτες και ξένοι.

tr.en: Some are selling, others are buying, others are talking about the war.
tr.el: Άλλοι πουλούν, άλλοι αγοράζουν, άλλοι μιλούν για τον πόλεμο.

tr.en: Dikaiopolis sells the oil and receives money.
tr.el: Ο Δικαιόπολις πουλά το λάδι και παίρνει χρήματα.

tr.en: Then Theodoros sees the Acropolis and is amazed.
tr.el: Έπειτα ο Θεόδωρος βλέπει την Ακρόπολη και θαυμάζει.

tr.en: "Father, what is that beautiful temple?"
tr.el: «Πατέρα, ποιος είναι εκείνος ο ωραίος ναός;»

tr.en: "It is the Parthenon, my child, the temple of Athena."
tr.el: «Είναι ο Παρθενώνας, παιδί μου, ο ναός της Αθηνάς.»

tr.en: So they climb up to the Acropolis and honour the goddess.
tr.el: Ανεβαίνουν λοιπόν στην Ακρόπολη και τιμούν τη θεά.

tr.en: From there they see the whole city and the sea.
tr.el: Από εκεί βλέπουν όλη την πόλη και τη θάλασσα.

tr.en: Finally they walk home, and Theodoros says:
tr.el: Στο τέλος περπατούν για το σπίτι, και ο Θεόδωρος λέει:

tr.en: "Father, how beautiful Athens is!"
tr.el: «Πατέρα, πόσο όμορφη είναι η Αθήνα!»

notes.n: Ἀθῆναι is plural, perhaps after the several settlements united under the Acropolis; Latin Athēnae is plural too. Modern Greek uses the singular, η Αθήνα.
ἔλαιον 'olive oil' (from ἐλαία 'olive') → Latin oleum → English oil. Modern Greek λάδι comes from the diminutive ἐλάδιον. βραδέως is the adverb of βραδύς 'slow': -ως makes adverbs, like English -ly.
ἥκω 'I have come, I am here' is present in form but perfect in meaning. ἀγορά 'gathering place, market' → Modern αγορά 'market', ἀγοράζω 'buy' (Modern αγοράζω); English agoraphobia.
πολίτης 'citizen' (from πόλις) is a masculine of the 1st declension, like Modern ο πολίτης; politics, police. τε … καί 'both … and'. ξένος 'stranger, guest' → xenophobia; Modern ξένος 'foreign'.
οἱ μέν … οἱ δέ … 'some … others …': the article working as a pronoun. πόλεμος 'war' → polemic; Modern πόλεμος.
ἀργύριον 'silver, money' (ἄργυρος) is cognate with Latin argentum, whence French argent 'money'. λαμβάνω 'take, receive' → Modern λαμβάνω (formal), παίρνω in speech.
ὁρᾷ: ὁράω is a contract verb, ὁρά-ει → ὁρᾷ. ἀκρόπολις = ἄκρος 'topmost' + πόλις. θαυμάζω 'wonder at' → Modern θαυμάζω, θαύμα 'miracle'.
ὦ πάτερ: ὦ + vocative is the polite way to address someone. τίς (always accented) asks 'who? which?'; ἐστιν, an enclitic, leans on it.

νεώς is the Attic form of ναός (the so-called Attic declension: νεώς, νεώ, νεῴ, νεών); Modern Greek uses ναός. Παρθενών is the temple of Athena Παρθένος 'the Maiden' (παρθένος → parthenogenesis; Modern παρθένα).
ἡ θεός: in Attic a goddess is often simply 'the god' with a feminine article. τιμῶσι from τιμάω 'honour' → Modern τιμώ, τιμή 'honour, price'.
θάλαττα shows Attic -ττ- where other dialects and Koine have -σσ-; Modern θάλασσα follows Koine. Compare πράττω / πράσσω.
ὡς + adjective makes an exclamation: 'how beautiful!' The adjective comes first and takes the stress.

title: A Visit to Delphi
author: Stemma
intro: Delphi, on the slopes of Mount Parnassus, was the seat of Apollo's oracle, consulted by cities and individuals from all over the Greek world; the god answered through his priestess, the Pythia. This story is told in the past. Look out for aorists, the simple past (ἔθυσεν, εἶδεν), and for middle verbs, whose passive-looking endings (-ετο, -ατο) carry an active or reflexive meaning.

tr.en: Dikaiopolis wanted to ask Apollo about peace.
tr.el: Ο Δικαιόπολις ήθελε να ρωτήσει τον Απόλλωνα για την ειρήνη.

tr.en: So he travelled to Delphi on foot; and the road was long and hard.
tr.el: Ταξίδευε λοιπόν με τα πόδια προς τους Δελφούς· ο δρόμος ήταν μακρύς και δύσκολος.

tr.en: At last he arrived at Delphi, where, as they say, the navel of the earth is.
tr.el: Τελικά έφτασε στους Δελφούς, όπου, όπως λένε, βρίσκεται ο ομφαλός της γης.

tr.en: First he washed in the Castalian spring, then he sacrificed a goat to the god.
tr.el: Πρώτα πλύθηκε στην Κασταλία πηγή κι έπειτα θυσίασε μια κατσίκα στον θεό.

tr.en: After this he went into the temple, where the Pythia sat on the tripod.
tr.el: Μετά από αυτά μπήκε στον ναό, όπου η Πυθία καθόταν πάνω στον τρίποδα.

tr.en: Dikaiopolis asked: "When will there be peace, Pythia?"
tr.el: Ο Δικαιόπολις ρώτησε: «Πότε θα γίνει ειρήνη, Πυθία;»

tr.en: The Pythia only answered: "Know yourself."
tr.el: Η Πυθία απάντησε μόνο: «Γνώρισε τον εαυτό σου.»

tr.en: Dikaiopolis was puzzled, for he did not understand the oracle.
tr.el: Ο Δικαιόπολις απόρησε, γιατί δεν κατάλαβε τον χρησμό.

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: But as he came out of the temple, he saw the very same letters on the wall:
tr.el: Βγαίνοντας όμως από τον ναό, είδε στον τοίχο γραμμένα τα ίδια λόγια:

tr.en: "Know yourself" and "Nothing in excess".
tr.el: «Γνώρισε τον εαυτό σου» και «Τίποτα σε υπερβολή».

tr.en: Then at last Dikaiopolis laughed and said:
tr.el: Τότε πια ο Δικαιόπολις γέλασε και είπε:

tr.en: "The god is wise: I must look for peace first within myself."
tr.el: «Σοφός ο θεός· γιατί την ειρήνη πρέπει να την αναζητήσω πρώτα μέσα μου.»

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: And so he went back home rejoicing.
tr.el: Κι έτσι γύρισε στο σπίτι του χαρούμενος.

notes.n: ἐβούλετο: βούλομαι is middle-only (a 'deponent'): passive-looking endings, active meaning. Modern Greek has many such verbs: έρχομαι, κάθομαι, θυμάμαι. ἐρωτῆσαι is an aorist infinitive; the aorist stem ἐρωτησ- shows the typical -σ-.
πορεύομαι 'travel, go' → Modern πορεία 'march, course'. πεζός 'on foot' (πούς, ποδός 'foot') → Modern πεζός 'pedestrian', πεζόδρομος; πεζή 'prose' (= on foot, not riding on metre).

ἀφίκετο is a strong (2nd) aorist middle of ἀφικνέομαι 'arrive': no -σ-, just a new stem ἱκ-. Delphi was the ὀμφαλός 'navel' of the earth; ὀμφαλός is cognate with Latin umbilīcus and English navel. Modern ομφαλός.

ἐλούσατο is a true middle: 'he washed himself' (active λούω 'wash someone'). Modern λούζομαι, λουτρό 'bathroom'. The -σα- aorist (ἔθυσεν, ἐλούσατο) is the direct ancestor of Modern aorists such as έλυσα, έγραψα.
τρίπους 'tripod' = τρι- + πούς 'foot'; πούς is cognate with Latin pēs and English foot. The Pythia sat on a bronze tripod over a cleft in the temple floor.
ἔσται 'will be' is the future of εἰμί. Modern Greek replaced the old one-word future with θα + verb (θα είναι), from θέλω ἵνα 'I want that'.
ἀπεκρίνατο: weak aorist middle of ἀποκρίνομαι 'answer'; Modern απόκριση 'reply'. Γνῶθι is the root aorist imperative of γιγνώσκω 'know', cognate with Latin (g)nōscō and English know.
ἔμαθε: aorist of μανθάνω 'learn, understand' (stem μαθ-) → μάθημα 'lesson', English mathematics; Modern μαθαίνω. χρησμός 'oracle' → Modern χρησμός.

νεώ is the genitive of νεώς (Attic declension). Ἐξελθών: aorist participle 'having gone out'; ἐξ-ελθ- uses the same stem as ἦλθον, the aorist of ἔρχομαι. τὰ αὐτά: αὐτός with the article means 'the same'.
The two most famous Delphic maxims were inscribed in the forecourt of the temple. μηδέν (μηδὲ ἕν 'not even one') uses μή, the negative of commands and wishes.
ἐμαυτῷ 'myself' = ἐμέ + αὐτός. δεῖ + infinitive: 'it is necessary to'. σοφός 'wise' → philosophy, sophist; Modern σοφός.
ἐπανῆλθε = ἐπ- + ἀν- + ἦλθε 'went back'. χαίρων is a present participle, 'rejoicing'; χαίρω → Modern χαίρω, χαρά 'joy', and the greeting χαίρετε.

title: In the Beginning Was the Word
author: Gospel of John
intro: The prologue of John's Gospel opens with a deliberate echo of Genesis, 'In the beginning…'. Its vocabulary is simple and repetitive, but λόγος, 'word, reason, account', carries centuries of Greek philosophy behind it. Almost every word here is still alive in Modern Greek, so a Greek speaker today can follow it without translation.

tr.en: In the beginning was the Word,
tr.el: Στην αρχή υπήρχε ο Λόγος,

tr.en: and the Word was with God,
tr.el: και ο Λόγος ήταν μαζί με τον Θεό,

tr.en: and the Word was God.
tr.el: και ο Λόγος ήταν Θεός.

tr.en: He was in the beginning with God.
tr.el: Αυτός ήταν στην αρχή μαζί με τον Θεό.

tr.en: All things came into being through him,
tr.el: Όλα έγιναν μέσω αυτού,

tr.en: and without him not one thing came into being that has come into being.
tr.el: και χωρίς αυτόν δεν έγινε τίποτα απ’ όσα έχουν γίνει.

tr.en: In him was life,
tr.el: Μέσα του υπήρχε ζωή,

tr.en: and the life was the light of humankind;
tr.el: και η ζωή ήταν το φως των ανθρώπων·

tr.en: and the light shines in the darkness,
tr.el: και το φως φέγγει μέσα στο σκοτάδι,

tr.en: and the darkness did not overcome it.
tr.el: και το σκοτάδι δεν το κατέβαλε.

notes.n: λόγος 'word, speech, reason, account' (λέγω 'say') → logic, -logy; Latin translates it verbum, and the Greek Church keeps ο Λόγος. ἀρχή 'beginning; rule' → archaic, monarchy; Modern αρχή. The opening echoes Genesis 1:1 in the Greek Septuagint: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός.
ἦν is the imperfect of εἰμί, 'was (continuously)'. Modern Greek ήταν continues it with a new ending.
πρὸς τὸν θεόν: πρός + accusative normally means 'towards'; here 'with, in the presence of'.
θεός without the article is the predicate: 'the Word was God'; ὁ λόγος, with the article, is the subject. Word order puts θεός first for emphasis. θεός → theology, atheist; Modern θεός.
οὗτος 'this one' picks up ὁ λόγος: 'he'.
πάντα 'all things' is neuter plural, and Greek puts a singular verb (ἐγένετο) with a neuter plural subject. δι’ αὐτοῦ: διά + genitive 'through'.

The punctuation followed here is the traditional one (also the Greek Church's). Modern critical editions put the full stop after οὐδὲ ἕν and join ὃ γέγονεν to what follows: 'What has come into being in him was life'. γέγονεν is the perfect of γίνομαι.
ζωή 'life' → Modern ζωή; zoology comes from the related ζῷον 'living being'. Latin vīta.
φῶς, φωτός 'light' → photo-, phosphorus 'light-bringer'; Modern φως.
σκοτία (classical σκότος) 'darkness' → Modern σκοτάδι. φαίνω 'bring to light, shine' → phenomenon, phantom; Modern φαίνομαι 'seem'.
κατέλαβεν: aorist of καταλαμβάνω 'seize, grasp', meaning both 'overcome' and 'comprehend' (Latin comprehendit). Modern καταλαβαίνω means 'understand'.

title: The Beatitudes
author: Gospel of Matthew
intro: The Beatitudes open the Sermon on the Mount. Every line has the same shape: μακάριοι + a group of people, then ὅτι + a promise, mostly in the future tense. Through their Latin form (beātī…) they gave English the word 'Beatitudes'.

tr.en: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
tr.el: Μακάριοι οι φτωχοί στο πνεύμα, γιατί δική τους είναι η βασιλεία των ουρανών.

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
tr.el: Μακάριοι όσοι πενθούν, γιατί αυτοί θα παρηγορηθούν.

tr.en: Blessed are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
tr.el: Μακάριοι οι πράοι, γιατί αυτοί θα κληρονομήσουν τη γη.

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. pl. m.
pres. act. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied.
tr.el: Μακάριοι όσοι πεινούν και διψούν για δικαιοσύνη, γιατί αυτοί θα χορτάσουν.

tr.en: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
tr.el: Μακάριοι οι ελεήμονες, γιατί αυτοί θα βρουν έλεος.

tr.en: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
tr.el: Μακάριοι οι καθαροί στην καρδιά, γιατί αυτοί θα δουν τον Θεό.

tr.en: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.
tr.el: Μακάριοι όσοι φέρνουν την ειρήνη, γιατί αυτοί θα ονομαστούν γιοι του Θεού.

w: perf. pass. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
tr.el: Μακάριοι όσοι έχουν διωχθεί για χάρη της δικαιοσύνης, γιατί δική τους είναι η βασιλεία των ουρανών.

notes.n: μακάριος 'blessed, happy' (Latin beātus); no verb is needed: 'Blessed (are)…'. Modern μακάριος means 'blissful, serene'. τῷ πνεύματι: dative of respect, 'in spirit'. πτωχός 'beggar, poor' → Modern φτωχός. πνεῦμα 'breath, spirit' → pneumatic; Modern πνεύμα.
αὐτῶν ἐστιν 'theirs is': a genitive of possession with εἰμί. ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν: Matthew's reverent way of saying 'the kingdom of God'.

οἱ πενθοῦντες: article + participle = 'those who mourn' (πένθος 'grief' → Modern πένθος). παρακληθήσονται: future passive of παρακαλέω 'call to one's side, comfort' (Παράκλητος 'the Paraclete'); Modern παρακαλώ 'please, I ask'.
πραεῖς is the plural of Koine πραΰς 'gentle, meek' (Attic πρᾷος). κληρονομέω 'inherit' = κλῆρος 'lot, share' + νέμω 'allot' → Modern κληρονομώ; English clergy comes from κλῆρος via Latin clērus.
χορτασθήσονται: future passive of χορτάζω 'feed, fill' (χόρτος 'fodder') → Modern χορταίνω 'be full', χόρτο 'grass'. δικαιοσύνη 'justice, righteousness' (δίκη) → Modern δικαιοσύνη.
ἐλεήμων 'merciful' from ἔλεος 'pity' → Κύριε ἐλέησον (Kyrie eleison); English alms via Latin eleēmosyna. The future passive endings -θήσονται recur through the whole passage.
καθαρός 'clean, pure' → catharsis; Modern καθαρός. τῇ καρδίᾳ 'in heart' (cardiac; Latin cor is a cognate). ὄψονται: the future of ὁράω comes from a different root, ὀπ- (optic, synopsis).
εἰρηνοποιός = εἰρήνη 'peace' + ποιέω 'make'; Latin pācificī. The name Irene comes from εἰρήνη. κληθήσονται: future passive of καλέω 'call'.

δεδιωγμένοι: perfect passive participle of διώκω 'pursue, persecute' → Modern διώκω, διωγμός 'persecution'. ἕνεκεν + genitive 'for the sake of'. The last line repeats the promise of the first, framing the whole series.

title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
author: Aesop
date: 6th c. BC (attrib.); prose collections of the Roman and Byzantine era
intro: The original of 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf': in Greek simply 'The Shepherd Who Played Tricks'. Its sentences are long, but built from a few repeated patterns: genitive absolutes ('when the villagers had rushed out…'), participles, and the impersonal συνέβη 'it happened'. The moral is one of the most quoted in Aesop.

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.
pres. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: A shepherd who drove his flock out rather far from a village kept amusing himself with the following game:
tr.el: Ένας βοσκός, που έβγαζε το κοπάδι του αρκετά μακριά από ένα χωριό, διασκέδαζε συνέχεια με το εξής παιχνίδι:

w: pres. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: calling the villagers to help, he would say that wolves had attacked the sheep.
tr.el: φώναζε τους χωρικούς σε βοήθεια και έλεγε ότι λύκοι είχαν επιτεθεί στα πρόβατα.

w: aor. pass. ptcp. gen. pl. m.
aor. act. ptcp. gen. pl. m.

tr.en: Two or three times the people from the village took fright and rushed out,
tr.el: Δυο και τρεις φορές οι άνθρωποι του χωριού τρόμαξαν κι έτρεξαν έξω,

w: aor. pass. ptcp. gen. pl. m.

tr.en: and then went away amid laughter;
tr.el: κι ύστερα έφυγαν μέσα στα γέλια·

tr.en: but in the end it happened that wolves really did attack.
tr.el: στο τέλος όμως έτυχε να επιτεθούν λύκοι στ’ αλήθεια.

w: pres. mid. ptcp. gen. pl. m.
pres. mid. ptcp. gen. sg. m.

tr.en: While they were cutting off sheep from the flock and the shepherd was calling the villagers to help,
tr.el: Ενώ εκείνοι ξέκοβαν πρόβατα από το κοπάδι και ο βοσκός καλούσε τους χωρικούς σε βοήθεια,

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: they, supposing he was joking as usual, paid less attention;
tr.el: εκείνοι νόμισαν πως αστειευόταν όπως συνήθιζε και δεν έδωσαν πολλή σημασία·

tr.en: and so it came about that he lost his sheep.
tr.el: κι έτσι κατέληξε να χάσει τα πρόβατά του.

tr.en: The story shows that this is what liars gain: not being believed even when they tell the truth.
tr.el: Ο μύθος δείχνει ότι οι ψεύτες κερδίζουν τούτο: να μην τους πιστεύουν ούτε όταν λένε την αλήθεια.

notes.n: ποιμήν 'shepherd' → Modern ποιμένας (learned; everyday βοσκός); its Latin equivalent pāstor gave 'pastor'. πορρωτέρω: comparative of the adverb πόρρω 'far'. διετέλει … χρώμενος: διατελέω + participle 'keep on doing'; χράομαι 'use' takes the dative (τοιαύτῃ παιδιᾷ).
κωμήτης 'villager' from κώμη 'village' (Modern κωμόπολη 'small town'). ἔλεγεν ὡς 'he said that'. ἐπῆλθον: aorist of ἐπέρχομαι 'come upon, attack'. βοήθεια 'help' → Modern βοήθεια, βοηθώ.

A genitive absolute with aorist participles: 'the villagers having been startled and having rushed out'. ἐκπλαγέντων from ἐκπλήττω 'strike out of one's wits' → Modern έκπληξη 'surprise'. δίς, τρίς 'twice, three times' (Latin bis, ter).
γέλως, γέλωτος 'laughter' → Modern γέλιο; γελάω → γελώ. ἀπαλλαγέντων 'going off, departing' (aorist passive of ἀπαλλάττω).
συνέβη 'it happened' (aorist of συμβαίνω) + accusative and infinitive; Modern συμβαίνει 'it happens', συμβάν 'event'. τὸ τελευταῖον 'finally'. τῇ ἀληθείᾳ 'in truth, really'.
Two more genitive absolutes: 'they (the wolves) cutting off the flock, and the shepherd calling'. ἀποτέμνω 'cut off' (τέμνω → anatomy, atom 'uncuttable').
ὑπολαβόντες 'supposing' (ὑπολαμβάνω). ἔθος 'custom, habit' → ethos, ethics; Modern έθιμο. φροντίζω 'take thought for' → Modern φροντίζω 'look after', φροντιστήριο 'cram school'.
στερέω 'deprive' takes the genitive of what one loses: τῶν προβάτων στερηθῆναι 'to be deprived of the sheep'. πρόβατον → Modern πρόβατο.

ψευδολόγος 'liar' (ψευδής 'false' + λέγω) → pseudo-, pseudonym; Modern ψεύτης. ἀληθεύω 'tell the truth'. τὸ μηδὲ … πιστεύεσθαι is an articular infinitive explaining τοῦτο. κερδαίνω 'gain' → Modern κερδίζω, κέρδος 'profit'.

title: The Fox and the Grapes
author: Aesop
date: 6th c. BC (attrib.); prose collections of the Roman and Byzantine era
intro: The fables attributed to Aesop, a 6th-century BC storyteller said to have been a slave on Samos, were retold in prose many times; the text here is Émile Chambry's standard edition. This one gave English the phrase 'sour grapes'. Like most Aesopic fables it ends with a moral, here introduced by Οὕτω καί 'in the same way'.

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. f.
pres. mid. ptcp. acc. pl. m.

tr.en: A hungry fox, when she saw bunches of grapes hanging from a vine trained up a tree,
tr.el: Μια πεινασμένη αλεπού, μόλις είδε τσαμπιά σταφύλια να κρέμονται από μια κληματαριά,

tr.en: wanted to get hold of them, but could not.
tr.el: θέλησε να τα φτάσει, αλλά δεν μπορούσε.

w: pres. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: As she went away, she said to herself:
tr.el: Καθώς έφευγε, είπε στον εαυτό της:

tr.en: "They're unripe."
tr.el: «Άγουρα είναι.»

w: pres. mid. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: In the same way some people, unable through their own weakness to achieve things,
tr.el: Έτσι και μερικοί άνθρωποι, όταν δεν μπορούν από αδυναμία να πετύχουν κάτι,

tr.en: blame the circumstances.
tr.el: ρίχνουν το φταίξιμο στις περιστάσεις.

notes.n: ἀλώπηξ 'fox' → Modern αλεπού (via a later form ἀλωποῦ); English alopecia, 'fox-mange' baldness. λιμώττουσα 'starving' is from λιμός 'hunger'. ὡς + aorist = 'when'.
ἐθεάσατο: aorist of θεάομαι 'gaze at' → θέατρον 'place for watching', theatre. βότρυς 'bunch of grapes' survives in botany (botryoid, Botrytis 'noble rot'); Modern Greek says τσαμπί.

ἠβουλήθη: βούλομαι forms its aorist with the passive-type ending -θη-. περιγενέσθαι 'get the better of, get hold of' takes a genitive (αὐτῶν). ἠδύνατο: imperfect of δύναμαι 'be able' (→ dynamic, dynamite).
Ἀπαλλαττομένη: middle participle of ἀπαλλάττω, 'taking herself off, going away'. εἶπεν is the aorist that serves λέγω 'say'.
ὄμφαξ 'unripe grape' (feminine). Modern Greek says αγουρίδα or άγουρο σταφύλι. Accent: ὄμφακες + the enclitic εἰσιν gives a second accent, ὄμφακές εἰσιν.
ἐφικέσθαι + genitive 'reach, attain'. ἀσθένεια 'weakness' (ἀ- + σθένος 'strength') → Modern ασθένεια 'illness'; English asthenia, myasthenia.
καιρός, the 'right moment', here 'the times, circumstances'; Modern καιρός 'time, weather'. αἰτιάομαι 'blame' from αἰτία 'cause, blame' → aetiology.

title: The Lord's Prayer
author: Gospel of Matthew
intro: The Lord's Prayer as given in Matthew 6:9–13, in the Koine Greek of the New Testament. It is recited daily in Greek churches, so every Greek speaker knows these words, though in the slightly different Byzantine text. Its string of commands (ἁγιασθήτω, ἐλθέτω, δός, ἄφες) is a compact lesson in the aorist imperative.

tr.en: Our Father in heaven,
tr.el: Πατέρα μας, που είσαι στους ουρανούς,

tr.en: may your name be held holy,
tr.el: ας αγιαστεί το όνομά σου,

tr.en: may your kingdom come,
tr.el: ας έρθει η βασιλεία σου,

tr.en: may your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.
tr.el: ας γίνει το θέλημά σου, όπως στον ουρανό, έτσι και στη γη.

tr.en: Give us today our daily bread,
tr.el: Δώσε μας σήμερα το καθημερινό μας ψωμί,

tr.en: and forgive us our debts,
tr.el: και συγχώρεσέ μας τα χρέη μας,

tr.en: as we too have forgiven our debtors,
tr.el: όπως κι εμείς συγχωρέσαμε όσους μας χρωστούν,

tr.en: and do not bring us into temptation,
tr.el: και μη μας φέρεις σε πειρασμό,

tr.en: but rescue us from the evil one.
tr.el: αλλά γλίτωσέ μας από τον πονηρό.

notes.n: Πάτερ is the vocative of πατήρ; Latin pater and English father are cognates. Greeks still begin the prayer with these words. The Byzantine text recited in church differs slightly: ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἀφίεμεν 'we forgive', and a closing doxology (ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία…).

ἁγιασθήτω 'let it be made holy' is a 3rd-person aorist passive imperative, a form Modern Greek has replaced with ας + subjunctive (ας αγιαστεί). Latin: sanctificētur nōmen tuum. ἅγιος 'holy' → Modern άγιος, Άγιο Όρος.
ἐλθέτω: aorist imperative of ἔρχομαι, built on the stem ἐλθ-; Latin adveniat rēgnum tuum. βασιλεία 'kingdom' (βασιλεύς 'king') → basilica, the name Basil.
γενηθήτω: Koine aorist passive of γίνομαι (Attic γίγνομαι, aorist ἐγενόμην). θέλημα 'will' from θέλω 'want' → Modern θέλημα. ὡς … καί 'as … so also'.

ἐπιούσιος occurs almost nowhere outside this prayer; it may mean 'for the coming day' or 'needed for existence'. Latin renders it quotīdiānum or supersubstantiālem. δός: aorist imperative of δίδωμι 'give', cognate with Latin dō, dōnum.
ἄφες: aorist imperative of ἀφίημι 'let go, release, forgive' → Modern αφήνω 'let, leave'. ὀφείλημα 'debt' from ὀφείλω 'owe' → Modern οφείλω, οφειλή.
ἀφήκαμεν is aorist: 'we have forgiven'; the Byzantine text has the present ἀφίεμεν 'we forgive'. ἡμεῖς is emphatic, 'we too'.

μή + aorist subjunctive expresses a prohibition: 'do not …'. εἰσενέγκῃς: aorist of εἰσφέρω, using the suppletive stem ἐνεγκ-. πειρασμός 'testing, temptation' (πειράζω) → Modern πειρασμός; English empirical and pirate share the root πειρ- 'try'.

ῥῦσαι: aorist middle imperative of ῥύομαι 'rescue'. τοῦ πονηροῦ can be neuter 'evil' or masculine 'the evil one'; the Greek Church understands the latter. πονηρός 'wicked' (from πόνος 'toil') means 'cunning, sly' in Modern Greek.

title: The North Wind and the Sun
author: Aesop
date: 6th c. BC (attrib.); prose collections of the Roman and Byzantine era
intro: A contest between the North Wind and the Sun, in the plain prose of the Aesopic collections. The story is built out of participles, especially genitive absolutes (τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀντεχομένου 'as the man held on'), the most typical construction of Greek narrative. Its moral, persuasion beats force, was retold by La Fontaine as 'Phébus et Borée'.

tr.en: The North Wind and the Sun were arguing about which was stronger.
tr.el: Ο Βοριάς και ο Ήλιος μάλωναν για το ποιος είναι πιο δυνατός.

tr.en: They decided to award the victory to whichever of them could strip a traveller of his clothes.
tr.el: Αποφάσισαν να δώσουν τη νίκη σε όποιον από τους δύο κατάφερνε να γδύσει έναν οδοιπόρο.

w: aor. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: The North Wind went first and blew violently;
tr.el: Ο Βοριάς ξεκίνησε πρώτος και φυσούσε με ορμή·

w: pres. mid. ptcp. gen. sg. m.

tr.en: and as the man clung to his clothing, he pressed him all the harder.
tr.el: κι όσο ο άνθρωπος κρατιόταν από τα ρούχα του, τόσο περισσότερο τον πίεζε.

w: pres. pass. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: But the man, worn down still more by the cold, kept putting on extra clothing,
tr.el: Εκείνος όμως, ταλαιπωρημένος ακόμη περισσότερο από το κρύο, φορούσε κι άλλα ρούχα,

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: until the North Wind grew tired and handed him over to the Sun.
tr.el: ώσπου ο Βοριάς κουράστηκε και τον παρέδωσε στον Ήλιο.

tr.en: The Sun at first shone on him moderately;
tr.el: Ο Ήλιος στην αρχή έλαμψε με μέτρο·

w: pres. mid. ptcp. gen. sg. m.

tr.en: and as the man took off his extra garments, he turned up the heat more fiercely,
tr.el: κι όταν ο άνθρωπος έβγαζε τα περιττά ρούχα, δυνάμωσε ακόμη περισσότερο τη ζέστη,

w: pres. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: until the man, unable to bear the heat,
tr.el: ώσπου ο άνθρωπος, μη μπορώντας ν’ αντέξει τη ζέστη,

w: aor. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.
pres. act. ptcp. gen. sg. m.

tr.en: stripped off and, since a river flowed nearby, went off to bathe.
tr.el: γδύθηκε και, αφού κυλούσε εκεί κοντά ένα ποτάμι, πήγε να λουστεί.

tr.en: The story shows that persuasion is often more effective than force.
tr.el: Ο μύθος δείχνει ότι συχνά η πειθώ είναι πιο αποτελεσματική από τη βία.

notes.n: βορέας 'north wind' → Modern βοριάς; English boreal, aurora borealis. ἥλιος → Modern ήλιος, helium, heliocentric; Latin sōl is a cognate. ἤριζον: imperfect of ἐρίζω 'quarrel' (ἔρις 'strife').

ἔδοξε αὐτοῖς 'it seemed good to them, they decided': the same formula opens Athenian decrees (ἔδοξε τῇ βουλῇ). ὃς ἄν + subjunctive = 'whoever'. ὁδοιπόρος 'traveller' (ὁδός 'road' + πόρος 'passage') → Modern οδοιπόρος.
ἀρξάμενος: aorist middle participle of ἄρχω, 'having begun'. σφοδρός 'violent, vehement' → Modern σφοδρός.
Genitive absolute: τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀντεχομένου 'with the man holding on'; ἀντέχομαι takes a genitive. ἐσθής 'clothing' → Modern εσθήτα 'dress' (formal).
ψῦχος 'cold' → Modern ψύχος, ψυγείο 'refrigerator'. περιττοτέραν is the comparative of περιττός 'beyond the usual, extra' → Modern περιττός 'superfluous; odd (number)'.
The words ὁ Βορέας are an editor's supplement in Chambry's text. παρέδωκε: aorist of παραδίδωμι 'hand over' → Modern παράδοση 'tradition' (a handing down).
Κἀκεῖνος = καὶ ἐκεῖνος, two words merged (crasis); the mark over α (the coronis) shows it. τὸ μὲν πρῶτον 'at first'. προσέλαμψε from λάμπω 'shine' → lamp; Modern λάμπω.

περισσά is the Koine spelling of Attic περιττά, used a line after περιττοτέραν: a sign of the mixed language of the fable collections. ἱμάτιον 'cloak' → Modern ιματισμός 'clothing'. καῦμα 'heat' (καίω 'burn') → caustic; Modern καύσωνας 'heatwave'.
ἕως οὗ 'until'. ἀλέα 'warmth'. ἀντέχειν 'hold out' → Modern αντέχω 'endure'.
ποταμοῦ παραρρέοντος: another genitive absolute, 'a river flowing past'. λουτρόν 'bath' (λούω, cognate with Latin lavō) → Modern λουτρό. ἀπῄει: imperfect of ἄπειμι 'go away' (from εἶμι 'go').

Articular infinitives: τὸ πείθειν 'persuading' and τοῦ βιάζεσθαι 'than forcing' (genitive of comparison). ἀνυτικός 'effective' (ἀνύω 'accomplish'). πείθω is cognate with Latin fīdō, fidēs; βία 'force' → Modern βία 'violence'.

title: The Tortoise and the Hare
author: Aesop
date: 6th c. BC (attrib.); prose collections of the Roman and Byzantine era
intro: The most famous race in literature, told in seven compact sentences. Each one pivots on participles that tell us what the characters did before the main verb: 'having fixed a time… they set off', 'having fallen down… he slept'. The moral uses a 'gnomic' aorist, the Greek way of stating a general truth.

tr.en: A tortoise and a hare were arguing about which of them was faster.
tr.el: Μια χελώνα κι ένας λαγός μάλωναν για το ποιος είναι πιο γρήγορος.

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: So they fixed a time and a place and set off.
tr.el: Όρισαν λοιπόν ώρα και τόπο και ξεκίνησαν.

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: The hare, relying on his natural speed, did not bother about the race,
tr.el: Ο λαγός, χάρη στη φυσική του ταχύτητα, αδιαφόρησε για τον αγώνα,

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: but lay down by the roadside and went to sleep.
tr.el: ξάπλωσε στην άκρη του δρόμου και κοιμόταν.

w: perf. act. ptcp. nom. sg. f.
pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: But the tortoise, well aware of her own slowness, never stopped running,
tr.el: Η χελώνα όμως, ξέροντας καλά πόσο αργή είναι, δεν σταμάτησε να τρέχει,

w: pres. mid. ptcp. acc. sg. m.
aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. f.

tr.en: and so, running past the sleeping hare, she reached the prize of victory.
tr.el: κι έτσι προσπέρασε τον λαγό που κοιμόταν και έφτασε στο βραβείο της νίκης.

w: pres. act. ptcp. acc. sg. f.

tr.en: The story shows that hard work often beats natural talent that grows careless.
tr.el: Ο μύθος δείχνει ότι συχνά ο κόπος νικά το ταλέντο που αμελεί.

notes.n: χελώνη → Modern χελώνα (and Chelonia, the zoological order of turtles). λαγωός (Attic λαγώς) → Modern λαγός. ὀξύτης 'quickness' from ὀξύς 'sharp, quick' → oxygen, paroxytone.
προθεσμία 'appointed time' → Modern προθεσμία 'deadline'. στήσαντες: weak aorist participle of ἵστημι 'set up, fix'. ἀπηλλάγησαν 'they got away, set off': aorist passive of ἀπαλλάττω.

μὲν οὖν … δέ contrasts the hare (here) with the tortoise (line 5). φυσικός 'natural' (φύσις) → physics; Modern φυσικός. ὠκύτης 'speed' from ὠκύς, as in Homer's πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς 'swift-footed Achilles'. δρόμος 'running, race' → hippodrome; Modern δρόμος 'road, street'.
πεσών: aorist participle of πίπτω 'fall'. ἐκοιμᾶτο: imperfect of κοιμάομαι 'sleep' → Modern κοιμάμαι; κοιμητήριον 'sleeping place' → cemetery. παρ’ ὁδόν 'beside the road' (elided παρά).

συνειδυῖα: perfect participle of σύνοιδα 'be conscious of' (σύν + οἶδα) → συνείδησις, Modern συνείδηση 'conscience' (Latin cōnscientia is built the same way: con- + scīre). οὐ διέλιπε τρέχουσα: διαλείπω + participle 'stop doing'.
παραδραμοῦσα: aorist participle of παρατρέχω 'run past' (aorist stem δραμ-, as in δρόμος). βραβεῖον 'prize' → Modern βραβείο 'award'.
ἐνίκησεν is a gnomic aorist: it states what typically happens ('often beats'). νίκη 'victory' (the goddess Nike). πόνος 'toil' → Modern πόνος 'pain'. φύσις 'nature' → physics, physiology.

title: Life Is Short, the Art Is Long
orig: ὁ βίος βραχύς, ἡ δὲ τέχνη μακρή
author: Hippocrates
source: Aphorisms 1.1; Oath (opening and the pledge on treatment)
intro: Hippocrates of Cos (c. 460–370 BC) became the symbolic father of Greek medicine; the treatises that go under his name were written in Ionic Greek by several generations of physicians. The first Aphorism, a sober summary of the doctor's task, became the Latin proverb ars longa, vita brevis. The Oath, still echoed at medical graduations, opens by calling the healing gods to witness and promises to use treatment only for the patient's good.

tr.en: Life is short, the art is long,
tr.el: Η ζωή είναι σύντομη, η τέχνη μακρά,

tr.en: the right moment fleeting, experience treacherous, judgement difficult.
tr.el: η κατάλληλη στιγμή φευγαλέα, η πείρα επισφαλής, η κρίση δύσκολη.

w: pres. act. ptcp. acc. pl. n.
pres. act. ptcp. acc. sg. m.

tr.en: The physician must not only be ready to do what is needed himself,
tr.el: Δεν αρκεί να είναι ο ίδιος ο γιατρός πρόθυμος να κάνει ό,τι χρειάζεται,

w: pres. act. ptcp. acc. sg. m.
pres. act. ptcp. acc. pl. m.

tr.en: but must make the patient, the attendants and outside circumstances play their part too.
tr.el: πρέπει να συμβάλλουν και ο ασθενής, και όσοι είναι παρόντες, και οι εξωτερικές συνθήκες.

tr.en: I swear by Apollo the Physician, by Asclepius, by Hygieia and by Panacea,
tr.el: Ορκίζομαι στον Απόλλωνα τον ιατρό, στον Ασκληπιό, στην Υγεία και στην Πανάκεια,

w: pres. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: and by all the gods and goddesses, making them my witnesses,
tr.el: και σε όλους τους θεούς και όλες τις θεές, παίρνοντάς τους για μάρτυρες,

tr.en: that I will fulfil, according to my ability and judgement, this oath and this written contract.
tr.el: ότι θα τηρήσω, όσο μπορώ και όπως κρίνω, αυτόν τον όρκο και αυτό το γραπτό συμβόλαιο.

w: pres. act. ptcp. gen. pl. m.

tr.en: I will apply treatment for the benefit of the sick according to my ability and judgement,
tr.el: Θα εφαρμόζω θεραπευτική αγωγή για την ωφέλεια των ασθενών, όσο μπορώ και όπως κρίνω,

tr.en: but I will keep them from harm and injustice.
tr.el: και θα τους προφυλάσσω από βλάβη και αδικία.

notes.n: Ionic: μακρή = Attic μακρά. Seneca's Latin made the saying proverbial: vīta brevis, ars longa. τέχνη is the 'art' or craft of medicine → technique, technology; Modern τέχνη 'art'. βραχύς is cognate with Latin brevis → brief, abbreviate; Modern βραχύς 'short' (βραχυπρόθεσμος 'short-term').

καιρός 'the critical moment' (Modern καιρός means 'weather' and 'time'). πεῖρα 'trial, experience' → ἐμπειρία, empirical; Latin perīculum 'trial, danger' is cognate. κρίσις 'decision', also the turning point of a disease → crisis, critical; Modern κρίση. ὀξύς 'sharp' → oxygen; Modern οξύς 'acute'.
ἑωυτόν: Ionic for ἑαυτόν. ποιεῦντα: Ionic contraction of ποιέοντα with εο > ευ (Attic ποιοῦντα). τὰ δέοντα 'what is needful', the participle of δεῖ 'it is necessary'.

νοσέοντα: uncontracted Ionic participle of νοσέω 'be ill' (νόσος 'disease'; Modern νόσος, νοσοκομείο 'hospital'). παρεόντας = Attic παρόντας 'those present'. ἔξωθεν 'from outside' (ἔξω 'out' → exotic).

The Oath. ἰητρόν = Attic ἰατρόν 'physician' → psychiatry, paediatrics; Modern ιατρός, γιατρός. Hygieia 'Health' (→ hygiene; Modern υγεία) and Panacea 'All-Healer' (→ panacea) are daughters of Asclepius, the god of medicine.
ἵστορας 'witnesses', from ἵστωρ 'one who knows' — the root of ἱστορία 'inquiry, history' and of οἶδα 'I know', Latin videō. ποιεύμενος = Attic ποιούμενος 'making (for myself)'.

ἐπιτελέα: uncontracted Ionic accusative of ἐπιτελής 'fulfilled' (Attic ἐπιτελῆ). συγγραφή 'written agreement' (Littré's text spells it ξυγγραφή; Modern συγγραφή 'writing of a book'). κατὰ δύναμιν 'as far as I can' → Modern κατά δύναμη.

A later clause of the Oath (the lines in between, on duties to one's teacher, are omitted). διαιτήματα 'regimens', from δίαιτα 'way of life' → diet; Modern δίαιτα. ὠφελείῃ: Ionic dative of ὠφέλεια 'benefit' (Modern ωφέλεια). καμνόντων 'the sick', literally 'those who toil' (κάμνω).

ἐπὶ δηλήσει … εἴρξειν 'I will keep (them) from harm': the idea later summed up in the Latin maxim prīmum nōn nocēre 'first, do no harm', which is not itself in the Oath. εἴρξειν: future infinitive of εἴργω 'shut out, keep away'. ἀδικίῃ: Ionic dative of ἀδικία 'wrong' (Modern αδικία 'injustice').

title: The Shepherds of Bethlehem
orig: Καὶ ποιμένες ἦσαν ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ
author: Gospel of Luke
intro: The angel's announcement to the shepherds near Bethlehem, read in churches at Christmas. Luke writes polished Koine with a Semitic flavour ('they feared a great fear'). The angels' hymn in the last two lines became the Latin Glōria in excelsīs Deō and opens the Greek Orthodox Doxology.

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: In that same region there were shepherds living out in the fields
tr.el: Στην ίδια περιοχή υπήρχαν βοσκοί που έμεναν στην ύπαιθρο

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: and keeping watch by night over their flock.
tr.el: και φύλαγαν με βάρδιες το κοπάδι τους τη νύχτα.

tr.en: And an angel of the Lord stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them,
tr.el: Και ένας άγγελος του Κυρίου στάθηκε μπροστά τους, και η δόξα του Κυρίου έλαμψε γύρω τους,

tr.en: and they were terrified.
tr.el: και φοβήθηκαν πάρα πολύ.

tr.en: And the angel said to them: "Do not be afraid;
tr.el: Και ο άγγελος τους είπε: «Μη φοβάστε·

tr.en: for look, I bring you good news of a great joy that will be for all the people:
tr.el: γιατί, να, σας φέρνω το χαρμόσυνο μήνυμα μιας μεγάλης χαράς, που θα είναι για όλο τον λαό:

tr.en: today in the city of David a saviour has been born to you, who is Christ the Lord.
tr.el: σήμερα γεννήθηκε για σας στην πόλη του Δαβίδ ένας σωτήρας, που είναι ο Χριστός, ο Κύριος.

tr.en: And this will be the sign for you:
tr.el: Και αυτό θα είναι για σας το σημάδι:

w: perf. pass. ptcp. acc. sg. n.
pres. mid. ptcp. acc. sg. n.

tr.en: you will find a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger."
tr.el: θα βρείτε ένα βρέφος τυλιγμένο σε σπάργανα και ξαπλωμένο σε μια φάτνη.»

tr.en: And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army,
tr.el: Και ξαφνικά εμφανίστηκε μαζί με τον άγγελο ένα πλήθος από την ουράνια στρατιά,

w: pres. act. ptcp. gen. pl. m.
pres. act. ptcp. gen. pl. m.

tr.en: praising God and saying:
tr.el: που υμνούσαν τον Θεό και έλεγαν:

tr.en: "Glory to God in the highest,
tr.el: «Δόξα στον Θεό στα ουράνια,

tr.en: and on earth peace among people of his good pleasure."
tr.el: και στη γη ειρήνη στους ανθρώπους που ευνοεί.»

notes.n: ἦσαν … ἀγραυλοῦντες: εἰμί + participle, 'were living in the open' (ἀγρός 'field' + αὐλή 'court'). ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ τῇ αὐτῇ: αὐτός after the article means 'the same'. χώρα 'land, region' → Modern χώρα 'country'. ποιμήν → Modern ποιμένας (learned), ποιμαντικός 'pastoral'.

φυλάσσοντες φυλακάς 'keeping watches': verb and object from the same root (figura etymologica). Koine -σσ- where Attic has -ττ- (φυλάττω). νύξ, νυκτός is cognate with Latin nox, noctis and English night; Modern νύχτα.

ἄγγελος 'messenger' → angel; Modern άγγελος. κύριος 'lord' → Kyrie; Modern κύριος also means 'Mr'. ἐπέστη: root aorist of ἐφίστημι 'stand by, appear'. δόξα 'glory' (also 'opinion', as in orthodoxy) → Modern δόξα. περιέλαμψεν: περί 'around' + λάμπω 'shine'.

ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν 'they feared a great fear': another figura etymologica, a Semitic-sounding emphasis. φόβος → phobia; Modern φόβος. ἐφοβήθησαν has a passive-type aorist ending but active meaning.
Μὴ φοβεῖσθε: μή + present imperative, 'stop being afraid'. Modern Greek says almost the same: Μη φοβάστε.

ἰδού 'look!' (an old imperative of εἶδον) → Modern ιδού. εὐαγγελίζομαι 'announce good news' (εὖ 'well' + ἄγγελος) → evangelist; Modern Ευαγγέλιο 'Gospel'. χαρά 'joy' → Modern χαρά. λαός 'people' → laity, lay; Modern λαός.

ἐτέχθη: aorist passive of τίκτω 'give birth' (τέκνον 'child'). σωτήρ 'saviour' → soteriology; the name Σωτήρης. χριστός 'anointed' (χρίω 'anoint') translates Hebrew Messiah; chrism. Δαυίδ is indeclinable; Modern Greek writes Δαβίδ.
No verb: 'this (is) the sign'. σημεῖον 'sign' → semantics, semaphore; Modern σημείο 'point, sign', σημάδι.

βρέφος 'baby' → Modern βρέφος, βρεφονηπιακός. ἐσπαργανωμένον: perfect passive participle of σπαργανόω 'swaddle' (Modern σπάργανα 'swaddling clothes'). κείμενον: participle of κεῖμαι 'lie'. φάτνη 'manger' → Modern φάτνη, the Christmas crib; Latin praesaepe.

ἐξαίφνης 'suddenly' → Modern ξαφνικά, ξαφνιάζω. πλῆθος 'multitude' → plethora; Modern πλήθος. στρατιά 'army' (στρατός → strategy). οὐράνιος 'heavenly' (οὐρανός → Uranus) is a two-ending adjective, so the masculine-looking οὐρανίου agrees with feminine στρατιᾶς.

αἰνούντων … λεγόντων are masculine plural participles, though πλῆθος and στρατιά are neuter and feminine singular: they agree with the sense, a host of angels (constructio ad sensum). αἰνέω 'praise' → Modern αίνοι, the hymns of Lauds.
ἐν ὑψίστοις 'in the highest (places)'; ὕψιστος is the superlative of ὑψηλός 'high' → Modern ύψιστος 'supreme'. Latin: Glōria in excelsīs Deō.

εὐδοκίας (genitive) is the reading of the oldest manuscripts: 'among people of (God's) good pleasure', i.e. those he favours. The Byzantine text used in the Greek Church reads εὐδοκία (nominative): 'and on earth peace, goodwill towards men'.

title: Two Sons of Darius
orig: Δαρείου καὶ Παρυσάτιδος γίγνονται παῖδες δύο
author: Xenophon
intro: Xenophon of Athens, a pupil of Socrates, joined the army of Greek mercenaries that the Persian prince Cyrus led inland against his brother, King Artaxerxes, in 401 BC. His Anabasis ('The March Up-Country') tells the story of the campaign and of the Ten Thousand's retreat to the sea. Its clear, plain Attic made it the classic first reading text for students of Greek; these are its opening sentences.

tr.en: Darius and Parysatis had two sons,
tr.el: Ο Δαρείος και η Παρύσατις αποκτούν δύο γιους,

tr.en: the elder Artaxerxes, the younger Cyrus.
tr.el: τον μεγαλύτερο Αρταξέρξη και τον μικρότερο Κύρο.

tr.en: When Darius was ill and suspected that the end of his life was near,
tr.el: Όταν ο Δαρείος ήταν άρρωστος και υποψιαζόταν ότι πλησίαζε το τέλος της ζωής του,

tr.en: he wanted both his sons to be with him.
tr.el: ήθελε να είναι κοντά του και οι δύο γιοι του.

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: The elder, as it happened, was there already;
tr.el: Ο μεγαλύτερος, λοιπόν, έτυχε να βρίσκεται ήδη εκεί·

tr.en: but Cyrus he summoned from the province of which he had made him satrap,
tr.el: τον Κύρο όμως τον καλεί από την επαρχία της οποίας τον είχε κάνει σατράπη,

tr.en: and he had also appointed him general of all the troops that muster in the plain of Castolus.
tr.el: και τον είχε ορίσει επίσης στρατηγό όλων όσων συγκεντρώνονται στην πεδιάδα της Καστωλού.

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: So Cyrus goes up country, taking Tissaphernes with him as a friend,
tr.el: Ανεβαίνει λοιπόν ο Κύρος στα ενδότερα, παίρνοντας μαζί του τον Τισσαφέρνη για φίλο,

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: and he went up with three hundred Greek hoplites,
tr.el: και ανέβηκε έχοντας μαζί του τριακόσιους Έλληνες οπλίτες

tr.en: and as their commander Xenias of Parrhasia.
tr.el: και αρχηγό τους τον Ξενία από την Παρρασία.

notes.n: γίγνονται 'are born': a historic present, typical of Xenophon's brisk narrative (so also μεταπέμπεται, ἀναβαίνει). Later Greek spelled the verb γίνομαι, the form that lives on in Modern γίνομαι 'become'.
πρεσβύτερος 'elder' gave Latin presbyter, whence Italian prete, French prêtre and English priest. νεώτερος, comparative of νέος 'young, new' (Latin novus, English new); Modern νεότερος.

ἠσθένει: imperfect of ἀσθενέω 'be weak, ill' (ἀ- 'not' + σθένος 'strength') → asthenia; Modern ασθενής 'patient', ασθένεια 'illness'. ὑποπτεύω 'suspect' → Modern ύποπτος 'suspicious'. τελευτή 'end' → Modern τελευταίος 'last'.

τὼ παῖδε ἀμφοτέρω: the dual, a special number for pairs. It was already old-fashioned in Xenophon's Attic and has vanished from Modern Greek. παρεῖναι 'to be present' (πάρειμι 'I am present', from εἰμί).
παρὼν ἐτύγχανε: τυγχάνω + participle = 'happen to be …'. Compare Modern τυχαίνει 'it happens', τύχη 'luck' and τυχερός 'lucky'.

ἧς is genitive because it depends on σατράπην: 'satrap of which'. σατράπης is a Persian word, Old Persian xšaçapāvan 'protector of the realm' → English satrap. μεταπέμπεται: the middle of μεταπέμπω means 'send for (someone to come to oneself)'.

ἀπέδειξε 'appointed' (ἀποδείκνυμι 'show forth, declare'). The plain of Castolus in Lydia was the mustering ground for the royal troops of western Asia Minor. ἁθροίζονται: Attic spelling with rough breathing of ἀθροίζω 'gather' (Modern αθροίζω 'add up', άθροισμα 'sum'). ἐς is the older form of εἰς 'into', which Xenophon often keeps.

ἀναβαίνει 'goes up', i.e. inland from the coast to the Persian heartland: the noun ἀνάβασις 'going up' is the title of the book. Modern ανεβαίνω 'go up, climb'. λαβών: aorist participle of λαμβάνω 'take'.
ὁπλῖται are heavy infantrymen, named after their ὅπλα 'arms, shield'; Modern οπλίτης is still 'soldier, private' and όπλο 'weapon'. τριακόσιοι 'three hundred'; Modern τριακόσιοι.

ἄρχων 'ruler, commander', the participle of ἄρχω used as a noun (at Athens the ἄρχοντες were the chief magistrates); Modern άρχοντας 'lord'. Παρράσιος: from Parrhasia in Arcadia — many of the later Ten Thousand were Arcadian mercenaries.

title: Equal to the Gods
author: Sappho
intro: Sappho of Lesbos, the most admired woman poet of antiquity, wrote in her native Aeolic dialect around 600 BC. In this poem she watches a man sitting close to the woman she loves and lists, symptom by symptom, how desire takes her body apart. It survives only because the critic known as 'Longinus' quoted it as a model of the sublime; Catullus translated it into Latin in his poem 51.

tr.en: He seems to me to be equal to the gods,
tr.el: Μου φαίνεται ίσος με τους θεούς

tr.en: that man, whoever he is, who sits opposite you
tr.el: εκείνος ο άντρας, όποιος κι αν είναι, που κάθεται απέναντί σου

w: pres. act. ptcp. gen. sg. f.

tr.en: and close beside you, as you sweetly
tr.el: κι από κοντά, καθώς γλυκά

w: pres. act. ptcp. gen. sg. f.

tr.en: speak, listens to you
tr.el: μιλάς, σε ακούει

w: pres. act. ptcp. gen. sg. f.

tr.en: and laugh so lovely — and that, I swear,
tr.el: και γελάς τόσο γοητευτικά — κι αυτό, αλήθεια,

tr.en: sets the heart in my breast fluttering;
tr.el: κάνει την καρδιά μου να φτερουγίζει στο στήθος·

tr.en: for whenever I glance at you, even for a moment, I can no longer
tr.el: γιατί μόλις σε κοιτάξω έστω και για λίγο, δεν μπορώ πια

tr.en: utter a single word,
tr.el: να βγάλω ούτε μια λέξη,

tr.en: but my tongue is broken and silent, and a thin
tr.el: μα η γλώσσα μου έχει σπάσει και σωπαίνει, κι ένα λεπτό

tr.en: fire has at once run racing under my skin,
tr.el: πυρ αμέσως έχει τρέξει κάτω από το δέρμα μου,

tr.en: with my eyes I see nothing, and my ears
tr.el: με τα μάτια μου δεν βλέπω τίποτα, και τ’ αυτιά μου

tr.en: are drumming,
tr.el: βουίζουν,

tr.en: sweat pours down over me, and trembling
tr.el: ιδρώτας με περιλούζει, και τρεμούλα

tr.en: seizes all of me; greener than grass
tr.el: με πιάνει ολόκληρη· πιο χλωμή κι από τη χλόη

tr.en: I am, and little short of dying
tr.el: είμαι, και λίγο λείπει να πεθάνω,

tr.en: I seem to myself.
tr.el: έτσι μου φαίνεται.

notes.n: The Aeolic dialect of Lesbos throws the accent back as far as possible (θέοισιν for θεοῖσιν, ἰμέροεν for ἱμερόεν) and has no rough breathing (ἰμέροεν, ὐπακούει, ἴδρως). κῆνος = ἐκεῖνος 'that (man)'. Catullus begins his Latin version Ille mī pār esse deō vidētur.
ἔμμεν’ = ἔμμεναι, the Aeolic infinitive of εἰμί (Attic εἶναι). ὤνηρ = ὁ ἀνήρ, article and noun merged by crasis. ὄττις = ὅστις, τοι = σοι. ἐνάντιος 'opposite' → Modern απέναντι, εναντίον.
ἰσδάνει = ἱζάνει 'sits' (Aeolic σδ for ζ). πλάσιον = πλησίον 'near' and ἆδυ = ἡδύ 'sweetly': Aeolic keeps the old long ā where Attic-Ionic has η. ἡδύς is cognate with Latin suāvis and English sweet.

φωνεί-σας is one word broken over the line-end: in Aeolic, contract verbs are inflected like -μι verbs (φώνημι), so the participle φωνείσας corresponds to Attic φωνούσης. ὐπακούω 'listen' later came to mean 'obey' (Modern υπακούω).
γελαίσας = Attic γελώσης 'laughing' (gen. with ὐπακούει). ἰμέροεν = ἱμερόεν 'lovely, desire-stirring', used as an adverb (ἵμερος 'longing'). μ’ here stands for μοι. ἦ μάν = ἦ μήν 'truly, I swear'.
ἐπτόαισεν = ἐπτόησεν, aorist of πτοέω 'flutter, excite' (Aeolic -αισ- for -ησ-). καρδία → cardiac; Modern καρδιά.

ὠς … ἴδω: Aeolic ὠς (= ὡς) + subjunctive 'whenever I look'. βρόχε’ = βρόχεα, Aeolic for βραχέα 'briefly'. φώναι-σ’ (over the line-end) = φώναισ(αι), Aeolic for φωνῆσαι 'to speak' (-αισ- for -ησ-, as in ἐπτόαισεν): literally 'nothing any longer comes to me to say'.

ἄκαν = ἀκήν 'in silence'. ἔαγε: perfect of ἄγνυμι 'break', 'is broken'. γλῶσσα is Aeolic and Ionic (Attic γλῶττα) → glossary; Modern γλώσσα. The text here, transmitted by a single manuscript, is uncertain.
ὐπαδεδρόμηκεν: perfect of ὑποτρέχω 'run under' (Aeolic ὐπα- = ὑπο-; δεδρόμηκα is the perfect of τρέχω, cf. δρόμος 'race, road'). χρῷ: dative of χρώς 'skin', related to χρῶμα 'colour' → chromatic.

ὀππάτεσσι: Aeolic dative plural of ὄππα = ὄμμα 'eye' (cf. ὄψις, optic, Latin oculus). ὄρημμ’ = ὁρῶ 'I see' (Aeolic ὄρημμι). ἐπιρρόμβεισι 'hum, drum', from ῥόμβος 'spinning top, bull-roarer' → rhombus.
ἄκουαι = ἀκοαί 'ears, hearing' → acoustic; Modern ακοή.

This line is corrupt in the manuscript (Lobel and Page print it between daggers: †έκαδε μ’ ἴδρως ψῦχρος κακχέεται†). κὰδ δέ μ’ ἴδρως κακχέεται, a widely printed restoration, keeps the transmitted verb and scans; others restore κὰδ δέ μ’ ἴδρως ψῦχρος ἔχει 'cold sweat holds me'. κακχέεται = καταχέεται 'pours down' (Aeolic κακ- for κατα- before χ), and κάδ is likewise the Aeolic short form of κατά. ἴδρως = ἱδρώς 'sweat' → Modern ιδρώτας.

παῖσαν = πᾶσαν 'all of me': the feminine shows the speaker is a woman. ἄγρει = αἱρεῖ 'seizes'. χλωροτέρα … ποίας: genitive of comparison, 'greener (paler) than grass'. χλωρός 'pale green' → chlorophyll, chlorine; Modern χλωρός 'fresh, green' and χλωμός 'pale'.
ἔμμι = εἰμί. τεθνάκην = τεθνηκέναι 'to be dead', perfect infinitive of θνῄσκω. ὀλίγω = ὀλίγου (Aeolic genitive -ω). ’πιδεύης = ἐπιδευής 'lacking', with the first vowel dropped (prodelision).
αὔτᾳ = αὐτῇ 'to myself'. A fifth stanza begins 'but all must be endured …' and then the quotation breaks off.

title: Ode to Man
author: Sophocles
intro: Sophocles' Antigone contains the most famous choral song in Greek tragedy, the 'Ode to Man'. Just after someone has defied King Creon's order and buried Polynices, the Theban elders marvel at human ingenuity — seafaring, farming, hunting, speech and city-building — while hinting that the same cleverness can lead to ruin. These lines are the first strophe, on the conquest of sea and earth.

tr.en: Many things are wondrous and terrible, but nothing is more wondrous than man;
tr.el: Πολλά είναι τα θαυμαστά και φοβερά, μα τίποτα δεν είναι πιο θαυμαστό από τον άνθρωπο·

tr.en: this creature crosses even the grey sea before the wintry south wind,
tr.el: αυτός περνά ακόμη και πέρα από τη γκρίζα θάλασσα με τον χειμωνιάτικο νοτιά,

tr.en: making his way beneath the swells
tr.el: προχωρεί κάτω από τα κύματα

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: that roar around him as he passes;
tr.el: που βρυχώνται γύρω του, καθώς τα διασχίζει·

tr.en: and the highest of the gods, Earth,
tr.el: και την ανώτατη από τους θεούς, τη Γη,

tr.en: eternal and untiring, he wears away,
tr.el: την άφθαρτη, την ακούραστη, την καταπονεί,

w: pres. mid. ptcp. gen. pl. n.

tr.en: as the ploughs turn back and forth year after year,
tr.el: καθώς τ’ αλέτρια πηγαινοέρχονται χρόνο με τον χρόνο,

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: turning up the soil with the offspring of horses.
tr.el: και την οργώνει με τη γενιά των αλόγων.

notes.n: δεινός means 'terrible', 'awe-inspiring' and 'clever' at once, and the ode plays on all three. κοὐδέν = καὶ οὐδέν (crasis). πέλει is a poetic word for 'is'. The word lives on in δεινόσαυρος, 'terrible lizard' (dinosaur), and in Modern δεινά 'misfortunes'.

τοῦτο 'this (creature)': neuter, because man is presented as a marvel, a 'thing'. πολιός 'grey' → poliomyelitis, inflammation of the 'grey' marrow. νότος 'south wind' → Modern νότος 'south', νοτιάς 'south wind'.
περιβρυχίοισιν … οἴδμασιν 'swells that roar around (him)': lyric verse keeps the old dative ending -οισι(ν). χωρέω 'go, make room' (χώρα 'space') → Modern χωράω 'fit'.
περῶν: participle of περάω 'cross', masculine although τοῦτο is neuter — the sense ('man') wins over the grammar. οἶδμα 'swell', from οἰδέω 'swell' → oedema. Modern περνάω 'pass' comes from περάω.

τὰν ὑπερτάταν, Γᾶν: choral lyric uses Doric ā where Attic has η (τὴν ὑπερτάτην Γῆν). Earth is the oldest of the gods. γῆ → geography, geology; Modern γη. ὑπέρτατος 'highest' is related to ὑπέρ, Latin super.
ἄφθιτον 'imperishable' (ἀ- + φθίνω 'waste away'; Modern φθίνω 'decline'). ἀκαμάταν 'untiring' (ἀ- + κάμνω 'toil'). ἀποτρύεται 'wears out' — the middle voice suggests he does it for his own profit.

ἰλλομένων ἀρότρων: genitive absolute, 'as ploughs turn to and fro'. ἄροτρον 'plough' is cognate with Latin arātrum and Old English erian 'to plough'; Modern αλέτρι descends from its diminutive ἀρότριον. ἔτος εἰς ἔτος 'year after year' (Modern έτος, formal).

ἱππείῳ γένει 'with the breed of horses', i.e. mules or horses drawing the plough. ἵππος → hippodrome, hippopotamus ('river horse'); Modern ιππικό 'cavalry', but everyday άλογο. πολεύω 'turn (the soil)'.

title: The Allegory of the Cave
orig: ἀπείκασον τοιούτῳ πάθει τὴν ἡμετέραν φύσιν
author: Plato
intro: At the start of Book 7 of the Republic, Socrates asks Glaucon to picture prisoners chained in a cave since childhood, who see nothing but shadows thrown on the wall by a fire behind them. The image stands for the human condition without education: we take shadows for reality until someone turns us towards the light. These opening lines set the scene for the most famous allegory in Western philosophy.

tr.en: Next, I said, compare our nature, in respect of education and the lack of it, to an experience like this.
tr.el: Ύστερα από αυτά, είπα, παρομοίασε τη φύση μας, ως προς την παιδεία και την έλλειψή της, με μια κατάσταση σαν κι αυτή.

tr.en: Picture men living, as it were, in an underground, cave-like dwelling,
tr.el: Φαντάσου ανθρώπους σαν να ζουν σε μια υπόγεια κατοικία που μοιάζει με σπηλιά,

w: perf. mid. ptcp. acc. sg. f.
pres. act. ptcp. dat. sg. f.

tr.en: with its entrance open to the light, a long one stretching the whole width of the cave;
tr.el: με την είσοδό της ανοιχτή προς το φως, να απλώνεται σε όλο το πλάτος της σπηλιάς·

tr.en: in it they have been since childhood, chained by the legs and the neck,
tr.el: εκεί μέσα βρίσκονται από παιδιά, αλυσοδεμένοι στα πόδια και στον λαιμό,

tr.en: so that they remain where they are and can only look straight ahead,
tr.el: ώστε να μένουν στο ίδιο σημείο και να κοιτάζουν μόνο μπροστά τους,

tr.en: unable, because of the chain, to turn their heads around;
tr.el: ανήμποροι, εξαιτίας των δεσμών, να γυρίσουν το κεφάλι τους γύρω·

w: pres. mid. ptcp. acc. sg. n.

tr.en: their light comes from a fire burning above and far off behind them;
tr.el: το φως τους έρχεται από μια φωτιά που καίει ψηλά και μακριά, πίσω τους·

tr.en: and between the fire and the prisoners, a road running higher up,
tr.el: κι ανάμεσα στη φωτιά και στους δεσμώτες, ένας δρόμος πιο ψηλά,

w: perf. pass. ptcp. acc. sg. n.

tr.en: and along it picture a low wall built,
tr.el: και κατά μήκος του φαντάσου ένα χαμηλό τοιχάκι χτισμένο,

tr.en: like the screens that puppeteers set up in front of the audience,
tr.el: όπως τα παραβάν που στήνουν οι θαυματοποιοί μπροστά στους θεατές,

tr.en: above which they show their tricks.
tr.el: πάνω από τα οποία δείχνουν τα θαύματά τους.

tr.en: I see, he said.
tr.el: Βλέπω, είπε.

notes.n: εἶπον 'I said': Socrates narrates the whole Republic in the first person. ἀπείκασον: aorist imperative of ἀπεικάζω 'liken', from εἰκών 'image' → icon; Modern εικόνα. παιδείας … πέρι: the preposition follows its noun (anastrophe) and throws its accent back. παιδεία 'education, culture' → encyclopaedia (ἐγκύκλιος παιδεία); Modern παιδεία.

ἰδέ 'look! picture!': aorist imperative of ὁράω (εἶδον), accented on the last syllable in Attic. The same root ϝιδ- gives εἶδος and ἰδέα, the 'Forms' that the allegory is about → idea. σπήλαιον 'cave' → speleology; Modern σπήλαιο, σπηλιά.

ἀναπεπταμένην: perfect participle of ἀναπετάννυμι 'spread open', 'standing wide open'. ἐχούσῃ agrees with οἰκήσει in the previous line: 'a dwelling having its entrance …'. μακράν 'long' agrees with εἴσοδον.
καὶ τὰ σκέλη καὶ τοὺς αὐχένας: accusatives of respect, 'in both legs and necks'. σκέλος 'leg' → isosceles 'equal-legged'. δεσμός 'bond, chain', δεσμώτης 'prisoner' → Modern δεσμός 'bond', δεσμώτης.
αὐτούς 'they' is the subject of the infinitives μένειν and ὁρᾶν (some editors read αὐτοῦ 'right there, on the spot'). τὸ πρόσθεν 'what is in front'. The infinitives depend on ὥστε 'so that'.
κύκλῳ 'round in a circle' → cycle; Modern κύκλος. κεφαλή 'head' → encephalitis; Modern κεφάλι. ἀδυνάτους agrees with the prisoners: 'being unable'.

φῶς … ὁδόν: still objects of ἰδέ 'picture (a light … a road)'. καόμενον: Attic κάω = καίω 'burn' → caustic, holocaust ('burnt whole'); Modern καίω. πῦρ 'fire' → pyre, pyromaniac; Modern πυρ (formal), but everyday φωτιά.

παρῳκοδομημένον: perfect passive participle of παροικοδομέω 'build alongside'. In the perfect the οι of οἰκοδομέω lengthens to ῳ (temporal augment). οἰκοδομέω 'build a house' → Modern οικοδομή 'building'. τειχίον 'little wall', diminutive of τεῖχος.
θαυματοποιοί 'wonder-makers': puppeteers and conjurors; Modern θαυματοποιός 'conjuror'. παραφράγματα 'screens, partitions', from φράσσω 'fence in'.
ἔφη 'he said': imperfect of φημί, the regular verb for reporting dialogue. The speaker is Glaucon, Plato's brother.

title: The Greatest Upheaval
author: Thucydides
intro: Thucydides, an Athenian general exiled after a failed campaign, began writing the history of the war between Athens and Sparta (431–404 BC) the moment it broke out. His first sentence names the author, the subject and the method, and claims that this war was the greatest upheaval the Greek world had ever seen. His dense, compressed Attic prose became the model of political history from Sallust to Hobbes.

tr.en: Thucydides, an Athenian, wrote the history of the war between the Peloponnesians and the Athenians,
tr.el: Ο Θουκυδίδης ο Αθηναίος συνέγραψε τον πόλεμο των Πελοποννησίων και των Αθηναίων,

tr.en: how they fought against each other,
tr.el: πώς πολέμησαν μεταξύ τους,

w: aor. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.
pres. mid. ptcp. gen. sg. m.

tr.en: beginning as soon as it broke out,
tr.el: αρχίζοντας αμέσως μόλις ξέσπασε,

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.
perf. mid. ptcp. gen. pl. m.

tr.en: and expecting that it would be great and more worth recording than any before it,
tr.el: και προσδοκώντας ότι θα ήταν μεγάλος και ο πιο αξιόλογος από όσους είχαν προηγηθεί,

w: pres. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.
pres. act. ptcp. nom. pl. m.

tr.en: judging from the fact that both sides went into it at their peak, fully prepared in every way,
tr.el: κρίνοντας από το ότι και οι δύο μπήκαν σ’ αυτόν στην ακμή τους, με κάθε προετοιμασία,

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.
pres. mid. ptcp. acc. sg. n.

tr.en: and seeing the rest of the Greek world taking sides with one party or the other,
tr.el: και βλέποντας τον υπόλοιπο ελληνικό κόσμο να συντάσσεται με τη μία ή την άλλη πλευρά,

w: pres. mid. ptcp. acc. sg. n.

tr.en: some at once, others at least intending to.
tr.el: άλλους αμέσως, κι άλλους με την πρόθεση να το κάνουν.

tr.en: For this proved to be the greatest upheaval that had ever befallen the Greeks
tr.el: Γιατί αυτή υπήρξε πράγματι η μεγαλύτερη αναστάτωση για τους Έλληνες

tr.en: and a part of the barbarians,
tr.el: και για ένα μέρος των βαρβάρων,

tr.en: and, so to speak, to the greater part of mankind.
tr.el: και, θα έλεγε κανείς, για το μεγαλύτερο μέρος της ανθρωπότητας.

notes.n: Like Herodotus, Thucydides names himself in the third person. ξυνέγραψε: old Attic ξύν for σύν; συγγράφω 'write up, compose' → Modern συγγραφέας 'author', σύγγραμμα 'treatise'. He calls it 'the war of the Peloponnesians and Athenians'; 'the Peloponnesian War' is our name for it.
καθισταμένου: genitive absolute with αὐτοῦ (the war) understood, 'as it was being set up'. ἀρξάμενος: the middle of ἄρχω means 'begin' (the active, 'rule' → monarchy, archon).

ἔσεσθαι: future infinitive of εἰμί after ἐλπίσας 'expecting'. ἀξιολογώτατον: superlative of ἀξιόλογος 'worth mentioning' (ἄξιος + λόγος); Modern αξιόλογος 'remarkable'. τῶν προγεγενημένων: genitive of comparison, 'than the wars that had happened before'.

ᾖσαν (with iota subscript) is the imperfect of εἶμι 'go', not ἦσαν 'they were': 'they went into it' (ἐς αὐτόν = the war). ἀκμάζοντες 'being at their peak' → ἀκμή, English acme, Modern ακμή. παρασκευή 'preparation'; in Christian usage the day of preparation for the Sabbath, so Modern Παρασκευή means 'Friday'.

τὸ ἄλλο Ἑλληνικόν 'the rest of the Greek (world)', a neuter adjective used as a collective noun. ξυνιστάμενον 'standing together, combining' (συνίστημι) → σύστημα, system; Modern συνιστώ 'recommend', σύσταση.
τὸ μὲν … τὸ δέ 'one part … another part'. διανοούμενον: 'having it in mind' (διάνοια 'thought'; Modern διάνοια 'intellect').
κίνησις 'movement, upheaval' → kinetic, cinema (κινηματογράφος); Modern κίνηση means 'movement' and 'traffic'. Thucydides claims his war outdid both the Trojan and the Persian Wars.
ὡς εἰπεῖν 'so to speak': a fixed phrase with the infinitive. Modern Greek has lost the infinitive and says θα έλεγε κανείς. ἐπὶ πλεῖστον ἀνθρώπων 'over most of mankind'.

title: The Inquiries of Herodotus
author: Herodotus
intro: Herodotus of Halicarnassus, whom Cicero called 'the father of history', wrote his account of the Persian Wars in the Ionic dialect around 430 BC. Its first sentence announces a new kind of book: an ἱστορίη, an 'inquiry', meant to save great deeds of Greeks and non-Greeks alike from oblivion and to find out why they went to war. He then starts with the stories the Persians themselves told about the origins of the quarrel.

tr.en: This is the setting-out of the inquiry of Herodotus of Halicarnassus,
tr.el: Αυτή είναι η παρουσίαση της έρευνας του Ηροδότου από την Αλικαρνασσό,

w: aor. mid. ptcp. nom. pl. n.

tr.en: so that what men have done may not fade with time,
tr.el: ώστε ούτε όσα έκαναν οι άνθρωποι να ξεθωριάσουν με τον χρόνο,

tr.en: nor great and marvellous deeds,
tr.el: ούτε τα μεγάλα και θαυμαστά έργα,

w: aor. pass. ptcp. nom. pl. n.

tr.en: some performed by Greeks, some by barbarians, may not lose their glory —
tr.el: άλλα από Έλληνες κι άλλα από βαρβάρους επιτελεσμένα, να μη μείνουν χωρίς δόξα —

tr.en: covering other matters and, above all, the reason why they made war on one another.
tr.el: και ανάμεσα στα άλλα, για ποια αιτία πολέμησαν μεταξύ τους.

tr.en: Now the learned men of the Persians say that the Phoenicians caused the quarrel;
tr.el: Οι λόγιοι των Περσών, λοιπόν, λένε ότι αίτιοι της διαφοράς έγιναν οι Φοίνικες·

w: pres. pass. ptcp. gen. sg. f.
aor. mid. ptcp. acc. pl. m.

tr.en: for these people came from the so-called Red Sea to this sea of ours,
tr.el: γιατί αυτοί, αφού ήρθαν από τη λεγόμενη Ερυθρά Θάλασσα σ’ αυτή εδώ τη θάλασσα,

w: aor. act. ptcp. acc. pl. m.

tr.en: and, after settling the land which they still inhabit today,
tr.el: και εγκαταστάθηκαν στον τόπο όπου κατοικούν και σήμερα,

tr.en: at once took to long sea voyages,
tr.el: αμέσως επιδόθηκαν σε μακρινά θαλασσινά ταξίδια,

w: pres. act. ptcp. acc. pl. m.

tr.en: and, carrying cargoes of Egyptian and Assyrian goods,
tr.el: και, μεταφέροντας φορτία αιγυπτιακά και ασσυριακά,

tr.en: they would put in at various places, and in particular at Argos.
tr.el: έφταναν σε διάφορα μέρη, και ιδιαίτερα στο Άργος.

notes.n: Herodotus writes Ionic: ἱστορίης = Attic ἱστορίας, ἀπόδεξις = ἀπόδειξις, Ἁλικαρνησσέος = Ἁλικαρνασσέως. ἱστορίη means 'inquiry, research'; through Latin historia it became Italian storia, English history and story. Modern ιστορία means both 'history' and 'story'.

The sentence has no verb: 'Of Herodotus of Halicarnassus, (his) inquiry's display (is) this', like a title page. ἀπόδεξις 'showing forth, publication' is the noun of ἀποδείκνυμι, the verb that returns in ἀποδεχθέντα (line 3).

ὡς μήτε … γένηται: purpose clause with the subjunctive. ἐξίτηλος 'faded', used of colours that wash out: Herodotus pictures memory as a dye that time bleaches. χρόνος → chronology; Modern χρόνος means both 'time' and 'year'.
θωμαστά: Ionic for θαυμαστά 'wonderful' (θαῦμα 'wonder'; Modern θαύμα, θαυμάζω 'admire').

Ἕλλησι … βαρβάροισι: datives of agent with the passive participle. βάρβαροι are simply 'people who do not speak Greek' (who seem to say 'bar-bar'); Herodotus gives their achievements equal weight. ἀκλεᾶ 'without κλέος (fame)': the epic aim of preserving glory passes to prose.
δι’ ἣν αἰτίην 'for what cause': αἰτία 'cause, responsibility' is the question of the whole work → aetiology; Modern αιτία. ἀλλήλοισι: Ionic dative plural -οισι = Attic -οις.

μέν νυν is Ionic for μὲν οὖν 'well then'. λόγιοι 'men learned in tales and records', from λόγος. Everything that follows depends on φασί 'they say': accusatives with infinitives (αἰτίους γενέσθαι, ἐπιθέσθαι, ἐσαπικνέεσθαι) — reported speech.

ἀπικομένους: Ionic has no aspiration (psilosis), so ἀπ- stands for Attic ἀφ- (ἀφικομένους). The 'Red Sea' (Modern Ερυθρά Θάλασσα) for Herodotus includes the Persian Gulf and the Indian Ocean. θάλασσα is the Ionic (and Modern) spelling; Attic writes θάλαττα.
τὸν καὶ νῦν οἰκέουσι: Ionic uses the article as a relative pronoun (τόν = ὅν). οἰκέουσι is uncontracted (Attic οἰκοῦσι); οἰκέω, οἶκος → economy, ecology; Modern οικία, οικονομία.
ναυτιλίῃσι μακρῇσι: Ionic dative plural -ῃσι. ναυτιλία 'seafaring', from ναύτης 'sailor' and ναῦς 'ship' (Latin nāvis) → nautical; Modern ναυτιλία 'shipping'.
ἀπαγινέοντας: Ionic ἀπαγινέω = Attic ἀπάγω 'carry away'. φορτία 'loads, cargoes' → Modern φορτίο 'load', φορτηγό 'lorry'.
ἐσαπικνέεσθαι: a double compound, ἐς + ἀπό + ἱκνέομαι, in uncontracted Ionic form (Attic εἰσαφικνεῖσθαι). τῇ τε ἄλλῃ 'to the rest (of the land)', i.e. to various places.

title: The Man of Many Turns
author: Homer
intro: The opening of the Odyssey, Homer's second epic, which follows Odysseus through ten years of wandering on his way home from Troy. Like the Iliad it begins with a single key word, ἄνδρα 'the man', and an appeal to the Muse, but the hero is not named until line 21. In ten lines the proem sets out the poem's themes: travel, endurance, homecoming, and the folly of the companions who die through their own fault.

tr.en: Tell me, Muse, of the man of many turns, who was driven
tr.el: Πες μου, Μούσα, για τον πολύτροπο άντρα που τόσο πολύ

tr.en: far and wide, after he had sacked the holy citadel of Troy;
tr.el: περιπλανήθηκε, αφού κούρσεψε το ιερό κάστρο της Τροίας·

tr.en: he saw the cities of many men and came to know their minds,
tr.el: είδε τις πόλεις πολλών ανθρώπων και γνώρισε τον τρόπο που σκέφτονται,

tr.en: and many were the pains he suffered in his heart upon the sea,
tr.el: και πολλά βάσανα υπέφερε στο πέλαγος μέσα στην καρδιά του,

w: pres. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: striving to win his own life and the homecoming of his comrades.
tr.el: πασχίζοντας να σώσει τη ζωή του και τον γυρισμό των συντρόφων του.

w: pres. mid. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: Even so he could not save his comrades, eager though he was;
tr.el: Μα ούτε κι έτσι μπόρεσε να σώσει τους συντρόφους, όσο κι αν το ήθελε·

tr.en: for they perished through their own reckless folly,
tr.el: γιατί χάθηκαν από τις δικές τους απερισκεψίες,

tr.en: the fools, who devoured the cattle of Helios Hyperion,
tr.el: οι ανόητοι, που κατασπάραξαν τα βόδια του Ήλιου Υπερίονα·

tr.en: and so the god took from them the day of their return.
tr.el: κι εκείνος τους στέρησε τη μέρα του γυρισμού.

tr.en: Of these things, goddess, daughter of Zeus, starting where you will, tell us too.
tr.el: Απ’ αυτά, θεά, κόρη του Δία, ξεκινώντας από όπου θέλεις, πες και σε μας.

notes.n: ἔννεπε 'tell' is an epic verb (ἐννέπω), from the same root as Latin inseque 'tell' and English say. πολύτροπος 'of many turns': much-travelled and endlessly resourceful at once; Modern πολύτροπος keeps the sense 'versatile'.

πλάγχθη: unaugmented aorist passive of πλάζω 'drive off course', related to πλανάω 'wander' → planet, 'wanderer'. Τροίης: Ionic -ης for Attic -ας. πτολίεθρον is an epic word built on πτόλις, the old form of πόλις.
ἴδεν = εἶδεν, aorist of ὁράω without augment; its root ϝιδ- is the same as in Latin videō and English wit. ἄστεα = ἄστη, plural of ἄστυ 'town'. νόον = νοῦν: Homer leaves vowels uncontracted.

ὅ γ’: in Homer the article is still a demonstrative pronoun, 'he'. πάθεν = ἔπαθεν (πάσχω) → πάθος, sympathy; Modern παθαίνω 'suffer'. ὃν κατὰ θυμόν 'in his own heart': ὅν here is the Homeric possessive ἑός/ὅς 'his own', cognate with Latin suus.
ἥν τε ψυχήν 'his own life', the same possessive. νόστος 'homecoming' is the theme of the whole poem; with ἄλγος it forms English nostalgia, 'the ache of homecoming', Modern νοσταλγία.

ὣς (accented ὥς, unlike the relative ὡς) = οὕτως 'thus'. ἑτάρους is the epic by-form of ἑταίρους 'comrades' (Modern εταίρος 'partner', εταιρεία 'company'). ἱέμενός περ 'though eager': περ makes the participle concessive, like Attic καίπερ.

σφετέρῃσιν ἀτασθαλίῃσιν: Ionic-epic dative plural -ῃσι(ν) = Attic -αις. The poem's moral appears at once: mortals suffer 'beyond their share' through their own recklessness, as Zeus says a few lines later.

κατὰ … ἤσθιον is tmesis: the prefix stands apart from its verb, giving κατήσθιον 'ate up'. βοῦς is feminine here: these are the Sun's cows. Ἠελίοιο: Homeric genitive in -οιο of Ἠέλιος = Attic ἥλιος → helium, heliocentric; Modern ήλιος.
αὐτὰρ ὁ 'but he', i.e. Helios. ἦμαρ is the epic word for ἡμέρα 'day'. νόστιμον ἦμαρ 'the day of return'; Modern νόστιμος has come to mean 'tasty'.

ἁμόθεν 'from some point or other': the Muse may begin wherever she likes. θύγατερ, vocative of θυγάτηρ, is cognate with English daughter; Modern θυγατέρα. εἰπέ is the aorist imperative of the verb 'say' (εἶπον serves as the aorist of λέγω).

title: The Oracle at Delphi
author: Plato
intro: In 399 BC Socrates was tried at Athens for impiety and corrupting the young; Plato's Apology is his version of the speech Socrates gave in his defence. Here Socrates explains where his reputation for 'wisdom' came from: his friend Chaerephon asked the Delphic oracle whether anyone was wiser than Socrates, and the answer was no. Puzzling over this riddle, Socrates says, set him on his lifelong mission of questioning others.

tr.en: You know Chaerephon, I suppose.
tr.el: Τον Χαιρεφώντα τον ξέρετε, υποθέτω.

tr.en: He was my friend from youth, and a friend of your democratic party too,
tr.el: Ήταν φίλος μου από τα νιάτα μας, αλλά και φίλος της δικής σας δημοκρατικής παράταξης,

tr.en: and he shared in that recent exile of yours and came back with you.
tr.el: και πήρε μέρος μαζί σας σ’ εκείνη την εξορία και γύρισε μαζί σας.

tr.en: And you know what Chaerephon was like, how impetuous in whatever he set out to do.
tr.el: Και ξέρετε τι άνθρωπος ήταν ο Χαιρεφών, πόσο ορμητικός σε ό,τι κι αν καταπιανόταν.

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: Well, once he went to Delphi and dared to ask the oracle this —
tr.el: Κάποτε λοιπόν πήγε στους Δελφούς και τόλμησε να ρωτήσει το μαντείο το εξής —

tr.en: and, as I said, gentlemen, please don't make a commotion —
tr.el: και, όπως είπα, μη θορυβείτε, άνδρες —

tr.en: he asked whether there was anyone wiser than me.
tr.el: ρώτησε λοιπόν αν υπάρχει κανείς σοφότερος από μένα.

tr.en: And the Pythia replied that no one was wiser.
tr.el: Και η Πυθία αποκρίθηκε ότι κανείς δεν είναι σοφότερος.

tr.en: His brother here will testify to you about this, since he himself has died.
tr.el: Γι’ αυτά θα σας δώσει μαρτυρία ο αδελφός του, που είναι εδώ, αφού εκείνος έχει πεθάνει.

tr.en: Now consider why I am telling you this:
tr.el: Σκεφτείτε τώρα για ποιο λόγο σας τα λέω αυτά·

tr.en: I am going to explain to you where the slander against me came from.
tr.el: γιατί πρόκειται να σας εξηγήσω από πού μου προήλθε η συκοφαντία.

w: aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: When I heard this, I pondered it like this:
tr.el: Όταν τα άκουσα αυτά, συλλογιζόμουν ως εξής·

tr.en: 'What on earth does the god mean, and what is he hinting at?
tr.el: «Τι άραγε εννοεί ο θεός, και τι υπαινίσσεται;

tr.en: For I am aware that I am not wise in anything, great or small;
tr.el: Γιατί εγώ ξέρω καλά ότι δεν είμαι σοφός, ούτε σε κάτι μεγάλο ούτε σε κάτι μικρό·

w: pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. m.

tr.en: so what can he mean by saying that I am the wisest?
tr.el: τι εννοεί λοιπόν όταν λέει ότι εγώ είμαι ο σοφότερος;

tr.en: He surely cannot be lying; that is not lawful for him.'
tr.el: Δεν μπορεί βέβαια να ψεύδεται· αυτό δεν του επιτρέπεται.»
